Latest Update: Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (448 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic on Tuesday disclosed more details about the biggest investment agreements with major cloud providers Amazon and Google.
  • While we already knew that Amazon stood to make a killing on its Anthropic investments from the IPO, Anthropic revealed that Amazon’s total stake will come in at just shy of 15% (14.7% to be exact).
  • According to recent reports, even more interesting is that Amazon could have, if it wished, owned an even bigger share of the organization.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic on Tuesday disclosed more details about the biggest investment agreements with major cloud providers Amazon and Google.

While we already knew that Amazon stood to make a killing on its Anthropic investments from the IPO, Anthropic revealed that Amazon’s total stake will come in at just shy of 15% (14.7% to be exact).

According to recent reports, even more interesting is that Amazon could have, if it wished, owned an even bigger share of the organization. When Amazon invested billions in Anthropic in 2023 and 2024 (long before Claude Code took the enterprise world by storm, back in the days when Anthropic looked like it would forever be a speck in OpenAI’s shadow), the cloud giant obtained promissory notes that could convert into equity.

In a recent development, these notes carry conversion prices of about $2.09 or $5.05 per share, depending on the year of investment. Amazon has opted to convert a chunk of them as part of the IPO into a special class of non-voting shares that will give it about 15% ownership. (The shares can receive dividends and convert to standard voting Class A shares when sold, the filing claims.).

But it has also opted to hold on to billions of dollars’ worth of the notes for now. If it converted them all right now, it would own just under 24% of Anthropic (23.8% to be precise).

Industry observers note that google, meanwhile, will own just under 14% (13.7%), also in non-voting shares, which come from the conversion of notes, as well as the “private placement” sale of shares as part of this IPO. A group of major tech companies (AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners) have agreed to buy $26 billion worth of this non-voting stock. Google and Nvidia each agreed to buy $10 billion worth.

So while a lot of investors stand to make billions of dollars in Anthropic’s IPO, Amazon is one of the biggest winners, and that doesn’t even count what AWS stands to earn from Anthropic’s commitment to spend more than $100 billion on its cloud services over the next decade.

Nvidia states it doesn’t plan to reappoint Jensen Huang as CEO

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Despite Nvidia founder and former CEO Jensen Huang’s recent offer to return to the chip firm he helped build from the ground up, the company is not looking to take him back.
  • Sources indicate that during the company’s earnings call on Tuesday, Nvidia chairman Harvey C.
  • “On November 12, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms,” Jones remarked, “Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite Nvidia founder and former CEO Jensen Huang’s recent offer to return to the chip firm he helped build from the ground up, the company is not looking to take him back.

Sources indicate that during the company’s earnings call on Tuesday, Nvidia chairman Harvey C. Jones told listeners that Huang’s return was not something that company leadership was considering.

“On November 12, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms,” Jones remarked, “Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member. The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”.

On Tuesday, Huang had posted on X that since he left the company, he has “seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” and added that “if the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”.

According to recent reports, huang resigned last week in dramatic fashion following revelations of a number of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who has been accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. That woman, former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, has maintained close ties to the former Nvidia CEO for years. Critics worry that the relationship may have influenced Nvidia’s dealings with China, and U.S. intelligence officials have expressed suspicions that she works for China’s Ministry of State Security.

The development has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry at a moment when the future of the AI business, in which Nvidia plays a pivotal role, hangs in the balance. It has also spurred investigations, including an independent investigation into Huang’s activities by Nvidia’s board and an SEC probe into Nvidia. Huang has been replaced by interim CEO Colette Kress, who is also the chipmaker’s chief financial officer and executive vice president, while the board searches for a permanent replacement. Jones added Tuesday that the firm was looking at both internal and external candidates.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that AI agents will ask far more questions of a tech giant's data than people ever did.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, AI agents will ask far more questions of a company's data than people ever did. Edelbyte is building the data platform that can answer all of them, fast and at a price that makes sense.

It has been revealed that AI agents will ask far more questions of a tech giant's data than people ever did. Edelbyte is building the data platform that can answer all of them, fast and at a price that makes sense.

In a recent development, last fall we got a message from Roy Reznik, one of the co-founders of Wiz, offering to introduce us to a team that had just left Microsoft. This was the only introduction to a founding team weâd ever received from Roy, and we paid attention.

According to recent reports, the people Roy wanted us to meet had built Kusto, a data engine that started more than a decade ago as a small incubation project inside Microsoft. Named after the oceanographer Jacques Cousteau because it was built for diving into oceans of data, Kusto was designed to get answers from enormous volumes of fast-arriving data, such as logs, telemetry and security events, in seconds rather than hours. It ran on a query language simple enough that anyone, not just substantial-data engineers, could use it. And it worked so well that it became the data engine underneath Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender and Azure Monitor, and was eventually offered to customers as Azure Data Explorer. Security teams in particular loved it, which is how Roy became one of its biggest champions. When we spoke with customers, large enterprises and fast-growing startups alike told us two things: it was game-changing data technology, and the team behind it was among the best theyâd ever worked with.

Industry observers note that avner Aharoni, Evgeney Ryzhyk, Alexander Sloutsky and Yoni Leibowitz were that team. Evgeney invented the Kusto engine and its query language, then rebuilt it three times, making it faster and cheaper with each iteration. Alexander turned half-formed ideas into finished features seemingly overnight, and Yoni made sure every complex design was fully thought through, starting before a line of code was ever written. Avner, who spent a quarter century at Microsoft, hustled Kusto from project to a globally beloved product. Their new firm, Edelbyte, builds on this success. We are proud to have led their seed round and to be their partners.

In B2B technology, this is a proven playbook: a team develops a solution inside a large company and then splits off to build it independently. Itâs the origin story of Sequoia portfolio companies such as Confluent, whose founders created Kafka at LinkedIn, and Temporal, whose founders built Cadence at Uber. Edelbyte now follows the same path.

But Edelbyte is not simply Kusto rebuilt for a fourth time; it is a rethinking, from first principles, of what a data platform should look like in the age of AI. With every major shift in computing, the way software is built changes, and the data infrastructure underneath it has to change too. Data platforms were designed around human consumers, and there is a natural limit on the number of questions one person can type in a day. That made the trade-offs, such as keeping less history so queries stay fast, asking fewer questions so the bill stays reasonable, and building the product inside whichever cloud the database happens to run in, easier to tolerate.

Recent findings suggest that but an AI agent investigating a problem is like a whole team of curious analysts who never get tired, testing multiple hypotheses concurrently. One agent might fire off fifty queries where a person would run one. And at that scale, rationing and trade-offs promptly constrain the true promise of AI. An agent is only as useful as the questions it can afford to ask, and what it can afford is decided in the data layer.

In a recent development, edelbyte keeps detailed history queryable at interactive speed, scales as data volumes and query demand grow, and gives people, applications and AI agents governed access to the same data. It brings search and analytics, which have historically been stitched together from separate systems at significant cost and complexity, together in a single platform. And it runs wherever you need it: in the cloud or on premises, managed or self-hosted.

The result is exactly what an AI-heavy workload needs: no more rationing curiosity, whether it comes from a person or an agent. Already, customers are seeing dramatic increases in efficiency, including tenfold increases in queries with no increase in budget.

Data platforms are among the most durable and lucrative businesses in technology, because data has gravity; once it accumulates in one place it rarely moves. Each era produces its own winners, and we believe the AI era will be won by the platform that lets builders, and the agents working for them, ask as many questions as they want without worrying about the speed or the bill. Edelbyte is building just such a platform, and we are thrilled to be part of the journey.

Nvidia says its open source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress reaffirmed the company’s commitment to open source AI during Tuesday’s earnings call with analysts — the first since CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation.
  • “At Nvidia, we are committed to fostering a vibrant open model ecosystem, so every country, manufacturer, and industry can build its own intelligence,” Kress remarked in her opening remarks.
  • Kress also spoke about Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face, a platform for open source AI models that the firm agreed to acquire for $12.9 billion in September, in what would be the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia’s history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress reaffirmed the company’s commitment to open source AI during Tuesday’s earnings call with analysts — the first since CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation.

“At Nvidia, we are committed to fostering a vibrant open model ecosystem, so every country, manufacturer, and industry can build its own intelligence,” Kress remarked in her opening remarks. She also noted that open models were accelerating AI adoption, citing a 35-fold year-over-year surge in weekly token volume on OpenRouter, including a 3.5-fold increase over the past three months.

Kress also spoke about Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face, a platform for open source AI models that the firm agreed to acquire for $12.9 billion in September, in what would be the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia’s history.

The platform, which serves more than 18 million developers and 200,000 companies, is still on track to join Nvidia, despite Huang’s ouster. Huang had heavily advocated for open source AI technology. His departure had raised questions about the tech giant’s future approach to open source AI models, with Hugging Face’s CEO calling Huang’s departure “a sad day,” and promising to “keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever.”.

So far, Nvidia’s prepares for Hugging Face appear unchanged. The acquisition was not directly addressed during the Q&A portion of the earnings call.

“Together, we will scale its platform and make intelligence more open, more capable, and more accessible,” mentioned Kress of Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face.

It has been revealed that last week, Nvidia founder Huang resigned from his position as CEO following news about his extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, an executive at the Singapore-based tech giant Megaspeed who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. He’s also accused of having extramarital affairs with two direct reports and is now set to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving. Meanwhile, the SEC is investigating Nvidia over whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, The WSJ reported.

Within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads. On today’s call, Kress noted that Nemotron is now the “most widely used U.S. open model on OpenRouter,” and it’s “where developers start to build their own intelligence.”.

“That foundation is empowering the ecosystem,” she mentioned.

Correction: Due to a typo, an earlier version of this article incorrectly stated the number of developers served by Hugging Face; it is 18 million, not 118 million.

#2974. Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (631 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (631 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the firm’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S.
  • China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an notable topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week.
  • Sources indicate that nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the firm’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.

China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an notable topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week. The disclosure comes the same day Nvidia declared it was creating a board-level committee to oversee national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks.

Sources indicate that nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump. The arrangement required the chips to be shipped through the U.S., allowing the government to collect a 25% tariff.

According to recent reports, the pathway angered China hawks who wanted to deny Chinese labs computing power and maintain the United States’ lead in AI, but Huang long argued that it was more important for the U.S. to compete in China. In April, he told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that “to concede that market for the United States technology industry is a disservice to our country.”.

Huang’s ouster — in part over an affair with the CEO of a organization under investigation for smuggling chips into China — has coincided with upcoming rules, issued Monday, barring advanced U.S. chips from foreign data centers that serve Chinese customers remotely.

Industry observers note that investment bank Jefferies forecast that those rules might trim between $44 billion and $62 billion from Nvidia’s data center revenue next year. Referencing the newly introduced export controls, Kress mentioned that the backlog of demand for advanced chips like Vera Rubin means the rules would have no impact on the firm’s top-line revenue.

In a recent development, in the long term, the manufacturer may face the loss of potential customers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia. Critics of Nvidia’s dependence on China claim that as much as 20% of its revenue comes from demand linked to the country — annual revenue at its Singapore subsidiary hit $104 billion in 2025 before Nvidia stopped disclosing those figures — but that’s clearly going to change.

Industry observers note that even before Nvidia decided to stop shipping H200s, China had largely refused to accept their delivery. The government would prefer to generate demand for the country’s domestic chip industry, even if major AI compute users want the still-superior Nvidia equipment, according to Jacob Feldgoise, a researcher at Georgetown’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology.

Meanwhile, Chinese frontier labs are finding ways to access Nvidia chips elsewhere. All of China’s leading AI models show evidence of having been trained on Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips that are prohibited from being exported to China.

That training may have taken place at data centers outside of China, but sales to those facilities will be barred under the fresh rules. If large data centers suited for training AI models want to buy Nvidia chips, they will have to certify they aren’t serving any Chinese customers, export control attorney Dan Fisher-Owens told TechCrunch.

If they can’t provide that certification, the new rules may force them toward other chip options and further eat into Nvidia’s market share.

Stripe backer Atomico calls for Europe to own its success stories

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that the report, for instance, notes that the likes of Black Forest Labs and Microagi have reached $100 million in revenue in months, not years.
  • Sources indicate that yet, there’s still more that the VC firm founded by Skype’s Niklas Zennström would like to see — and its call this year is for Europe to “build it” and “scale it,” but also “own it.” That’s a way of wishing these companies will remain European longer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Europe is home to many of the world’s fastest growing companies of all time, veteran VC firm Atomico highlighted in its latest annual State of European Tech report.

It has been revealed that the report, for instance, notes that the likes of Black Forest Labs and Microagi have reached $100 million in revenue in months, not years. “I think we can put to bed the idea that there’s a fundamental reason or constraint on the ability to scale a breakout company from here in Europe,” Atomico partner and head of intelligence Tom Wehmeier (pictured) told TechCrunch.

Sources indicate that yet, there’s still more that the VC firm founded by Skype’s Niklas Zennström would like to see — and its call this year is for Europe to “build it” and “scale it,” but also “own it.” That’s a way of wishing these companies will remain European longer. But there’s also a sense that this success hasn’t been acknowledged enough, perhaps obscured by louder calls for improvements.

Wehmeier, the report’s lead author, was quick to opine that “policy, procurement and capital are not moving at the same speed as our founders.” But he mentioned the tech sector should advocate for itself in an inspiring way.

“When it comes to policy, I think the language needs to be, ‘Hey, this is not us complaining. This is us saying here is an opportunity to make the magnitude of impact even greater,’” Wehmeier said. “When we frame it as problems, that becomes harder.”.

This reframing may also help European tech improve its image abroad, where complaints around overregulation may have overshadowed Europe’s potential to leverage its deep tech talent and growing pool of repeat entrepreneurs to have even more of success stories.

Plenty could be still done to fully unlock this potential, and Wehmeier remarked that “the next few weeks are going to be a really important test, with EU Inc.” Also known as the 28th regime, this initiative would create a unified European corporate regime akin to the Delaware C Corp.

In a recent development, if the last stretch of EU Inc’s grassroots campaign achieves it goal, it will become much easier to create and operate businesses across the EU. It would also show that the tech system got itself heard, which could open the door to the kind of endorsement Atomico is hoping to see more of.

In a recent development, politicians have strong incentives to give the tech sector what it wants. If it is Europe’s second largest sector, biggest contributor to growth, and biggest job creator, “Do we not want more of that?” Wehmeier asked rhetorically. But it is unclear whether it will win them any votes.

Industry observers note that to make the answer more straightforward, the tech sector will have to work on having public opinion on its side. For Wehmeier, one key is to “demonstrate that this is translating into value for citizens.”.

The report is supporting this endeavor with a mix of high-level data and examples from its portfolio; for instance, it notes that ICEYE’s satellites monitor severe weather, flooding, and other hazards; and Daniel Ek’s Neko Health has now done more than 100,000 body scans, some of which helped identify severe or life-threatening health conditions.

One limit to this argument is that Neko Health’s scans will seem pricey to most Europeans, who largely rely on collective, public health insurance. But Atomico seems to hope that its report will give readers FOMO not just as potential customers, but also as potential shareholders.

Recent findings suggest that there’s more to be done for this to happen. Beyond joining the sector’s push for an EU capital markets union, he hopes more of Europe’s institutional investors will invest in the region’s own tech companies. “We must get to the place where Europe and European beneficiaries are the biggest shareholders in the success that we create,” Wehmeier remarked.

According to recent reports, before that can happen, the industry must overcome anti-industry beliefs like fears of AI-induced job destruction. But Wehmeier is a believer in the power of proof. “I think that trust is going to be earned through showing results to the public — be that lower energy bills, better healthcare, more homes built for cheaper and faster, and having infrastructure that we can rely on.”.

Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (475 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Despite the turmoil at Nvidia following the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company — as expected — delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday.
  • On Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the year-ago quarter and a beat above the company’s guidance.
  • She also said full-year revenue is on track to exceed expectations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite the turmoil at Nvidia following the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company — as expected — delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday. More importantly, Nvidia reassured investors that its streak of record-breaking revenue won’t stop.

On Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the year-ago quarter and a beat above the company’s guidance. Nvidia had told Wall Street to expect $108 billion in revenue for its third quarter of fiscal 2027. Kress also projected an even bigger fourth quarter, with revenue expected to reach $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.

She also said full-year revenue is on track to exceed expectations.

Sources indicate that “We are raising our fiscal year 2028 outlook. We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% and off what is now a higher fiscal 2027 base,” Kress said on the quarterly conference call on Tuesday. “Our outlook considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital.”.

Sources indicate that the company also reminded investors that it was using some of its billions in cash to buy back shares. In September 2026, Nvidia increased its share buyback program by $150 billion. It spent $28.1 billion on its own shares during the quarter and still had another $227.3 billion remaining in the kitty for additional repurchases.

Ironically, Nvidia could also benefit from the plunge in its share price following Huang’s resignation last week, should shares remain depressed over the longer term. The stock is down about 10% since his departure. Investors, however, celebrated Tuesday’s quarterly results, sending shares up about 4% in after-hours trading.

Kress stressed that the organization was in good shape now and for the foreseeable future, even without Huang at the helm.

Recent findings suggest that “We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress stressed. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.”.

She added that the organization has secured memory and advanced packaging capacity and is working with its chip manufacturer, TSMC, to “narrow the supply and demand gaps.”.

#2970. Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt

📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (651 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: it revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday, up from the $22 billion reported in January.
  • The company invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it mentioned, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year.
  • But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: it revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday, up from the $22 billion reported in January. The increase includes both new investments and significant markups of existing portfolio companies.

The company invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it mentioned, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year. This amount includes buying shares in public and private companies, yet it indicates how the chipmaker made massive bets over the course of the year, especially compared to last year; in November 2025, the company reported spending $5 billion buying equity in the first nine months of that fiscal year.

But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia stated in late 2023 that the goal of its corporate investing is to expand the AI ecosystem by backing startups it considers to be “game changers and market makers.”  Over the nearly three years that followed, the chipmaker has invested in nearly 350 startups, according to PitchBook. The companies Nvidia backed include Anthropic, OpenAI; neolabs like Thinking Machines and Reflection; neoclouds, like Lambda, Nscale, and Crusoe; as well as other companies developing AI infrastructure, robotics startups, and applications.

It’s also become a big financier of the data center build out, reporting $118 billion in guarantees with $105 billion of that the backstop it supplied for OpenAI’s $500 billion data center in Ohio.

The company made those commitments by allocating a meaningful portion of its excess cash flows. In Tuesday’s earning call, Kress said Nvidia would continue providing financing assistance to strong customers and that “as the market matures and additional sources of capital become available,” the company would be “rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees.”.

But the question for the VC ecosystem is whether the company will continue to back startups at anywhere near the same level without Huang at the helm.

Industry observers note that huang’s rampant dealmaking has reportedly been a source of concern for Kress. Investors have told TechCrunch that they anticipate that she will take a more conservative approach to startup investing, becoming more selective with newly introduced investments and writing smaller-sized checks into its existing portfolio companies.

“We intend to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses to shareholders during this last quarter and going forward,” Kress remarked on the earnings call on Tuesday. Just how strategic startups will be under her leadership, and under the future permanent CEO, remains to be seen. But for now, VCs are bracing for a meaningful pullback in capital.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google’s Pixel Tag, the firm’s take on an Android-exclusive Bluetooth tracker, is finally here, following its August announcement during the Google I/O developer conference.
  • Also: Google’s latest Android XR glasses have lower ‘creep factor’ than competitors.
  • Pixel Tag is a complete Bluetooth tracker for Android owners that appears less confined to device-specific ecosystems than Samsung’s Smart Tag 3 and Apple’s AirTag.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Pixel Tag, the firm’s take on an Android-exclusive Bluetooth tracker, is finally here, following its August announcement during the Google I/O developer conference.

Also: Google’s latest Android XR glasses have lower ‘creep factor’ than competitors.

Pixel Tag is a complete Bluetooth tracker for Android owners that appears less confined to device-specific ecosystems than Samsung’s Smart Tag 3 and Apple’s AirTag.

Sources indicate that however, if you look at Google’s footnotes, the Pixel Tag’s functionality is diminished when an older Android phone is involved. Several of the tracker’s best features require a compatible device running Android 9.0+ and Bluetooth 6.0+, according to Google.

Android 9 and newer encompasses a lot of devices, but Bluetooth 6.0 and newer doesn’t. Here’s what to check before you buy.

Industry observers note that smartphones began shipping with Bluetooth 6.0 in 2025, starting with the Samsung Galaxy S26 Plus and Galaxy S26 Ultra. The following phones also have Bluetooth 6.0:.

If your Android phone is older than any of the listed above, even by a generation, it likely supports Bluetooth 5.3 or 5.4 — not enough for the Pixel Tag’s best features.

Sources indicate that the Pixel Tag’s precision-finding capabilities are powered by Bluetooth Channel Sounding, a key feature introduced in Bluetooth 6.0. Nearly every review I’ve seen of the Pixel Tag, including our own, tests the tracker when paired with a Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 11, or Pixel 11 Pro.

It has been revealed that I assume that Android owners whose phones run Android 9.0+ but lack Bluetooth 6.0+ can use the Pixel Tag for very basic, general location tracking. These users may see the tracker’s general location, but Google’s device compatibility footnote appears several times throughout its press release.

The following features require Android 9.0+ and Bluetooth 6.0+, according to Google’s release:.

So, on older Android devices without Android 9.0+ and Bluetooth 6.0+, the following aren’t supported: locating the exact direction and distance of your tracked devices, pinging a tracker when you don’t see it, or giving your tracked devices a custom name.

Also: 3 ways Bluetooth 7 upgrades your devices beyond lossless audio.

Additionally, shorter-distance tracking requires an ultra-wideband chip inside your Android phone. Channel Sounding handles distance and direction at longer ranges, while UWB takes over for shorter ranges. Most premium Android phones with Bluetooth 6.0 also have UWB chips, but several of Google’s base-model phones lack a UWB chip.

Samsung’s base-model, A-series, and Z Flip-series phones also lack UWB, resulting in more phones that can’t access the Pixel Tag’s short-range precision finding capabilities.

Recent findings suggest that with all the specs in mind, the Pixel Tag is the best option for users of recent premium flagship Android phones. Those without the latest Bluetooth connectivity will find that the Pixel Tag works like any other Bluetooth tracker, with basic functionality.

Also: These are the closest things to AirTags for Android customers.

Sources indicate that the good thing is that a single Pixel Tag is $30, so it’s not much more expensive than a Tile Tag, and cheaper than a Chipolo Loop. Still, if your phone doesn’t support Bluetooth 6.0, you might be better off looking for a cheaper option until you’re ready to upgrade.

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (347 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google is adding digital home keys to Google Wallet, letting owners tap their phones to unlock compatible smart locks.
  • Also: This tiny box gives your older tech smart home superpowers.
  • Recent findings suggest that apple introduced Home Keys in 2021 with iOS 15, allowing customers to store digital keys in the Apple Wallet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google is adding digital home keys to Google Wallet, letting owners tap their phones to unlock compatible smart locks. The home key functionality, which will integrate with Google Home, will roll out this month.

Also: This tiny box gives your older tech smart home superpowers.

Recent findings suggest that apple introduced Home Keys in 2021 with iOS 15, allowing customers to store digital keys in the Apple Wallet. This lets you tap your iPhone or Apple Watch on the lock to unlock it. More recently, the addition of Express Mode to Apple Home lets users unlock smart locks without first unlocking their iPhones with Face ID.

Industry observers note that google’s digital keys use tap-to-unlock via NFC on smart locks. Like the Apple Home Key, you don’t need to unlock your phone to use your digital key, though you can change your verification settings as you wish.

Industry observers note that google’s announcement confirms that the company is embracing Aliro and UWB unlocking technologies as well. UWB unlocking for smart locks is supported on Google Pixel 10 Pro and newer models, as well as select UWB-enabled Samsung Galaxy phones. Aliro is a common standard for compatible smart locks and devices.

Industry observers note that before Google’s announcement, compatible smart locks could be controlled on Android through their accompanying app and Google Home. Smart lock companies also offered their own digital access methods, like NFC cards, Bluetooth, and geolocation.

Recent findings suggest that one digital key will be created for each Google Home, so it can unlock all compatible smart locks in that home. You won’t need to search through digital keys in Google Wallet to find the one for your front door, back door, or bedroom door — just tap your phone and Google Home will recognize the lock as one in your smart home ecosystem.

At launch, Google Wallet will support digital keys for the Aqara U400 with UWB and NFC, and NFC on the Schlage Sense Pro and Nuki Keypad 2.

Google Wallet already supports digital car keys for compatible vehicles.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In an exclusive first reported by freelance journalist Janko Roettgers via his newsletter, Lowpass, the streaming device maker confirmed it won’t be making any additional smart home products going forward, as its existing home devices run out of stock.
  • It has been revealed that “We’re sharpening our focus on Roku’s core mission: being the top streaming platform,” a Roku spokesperson told Roettgers via email.
  • Also: Worried about Fox buying Roku?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roku is stepping back from smart home gear.

In an exclusive first reported by freelance journalist Janko Roettgers via his newsletter, Lowpass, the streaming device maker confirmed it won’t be making any additional smart home products going forward, as its existing home devices run out of stock.

It has been revealed that “We’re sharpening our focus on Roku’s core mission: being the top streaming platform,” a Roku spokesperson told Roettgers via email. “As part of that, we plan to wind down sales of smart home hardware and will provide continued support and services for Roku Smart Home products.”.

Also: Worried about Fox buying Roku? Here are three popular concerns – and why I’m optimistic.

Roku was recently acquired by Fox, with the formal sale closing on Nov. 6.

Roku, primarily known for its streaming stick and TV devices that rival competitors like Amazon’s Fire lineup, expanded into the smart home space in 2022 with a series of affordable home security cameras, smart plugs, and lights, developed with white-labeled hardware from Waze. Roku introduced its own product lineup with proprietary hardware in 2025.

Also: Roku is taking away a fan-favorite screensaver – but you have alternatives.

Sources indicate that in 2024, the manufacturer launched TV features connected to its smart home products, including a view that let users cycle through their live camera feeds on their TV and a picture-in-picture feature that pins a feed to your screen while users have another app open. It’s unclear how this change will impact support for these cameras and associated features for those who already own them, but ZDNET has reached out to Roku for comment.

Roettgers mentioned in his newsletter that, based on Roku’s own website, the number of products available for purchase appears to have dwindled. Currently, all but two of Roku’s smart home gear are listed as out of stock.

At other retailers like Home Depot, Amazon, and Walmart, many Roku listings have been removed or marked for clearance, while some retailers are only selling refurbished items.

It’s likely, as Roettgers identified in a previous newsletter, that Fox did not see long-term value in smart home gear for Roku, a fact certainly exacerbated by AI-induced hardware cost increases that have hit nearly every tech manufacturer, including Apple.

Also: Why your RAM options cost 4X more now than last year – even legacy tech prices aren’t immune.

The closure of the sale of Roku to Fox also emphasizes the return to streaming as the company’s main priority. Roettgers mentioned the reason for that has been publicly noted in Roku’s financial disclosures, including last week’s 10-Q, where the brand clearly emphasized that smart home gear does not contribute to Roku’s streaming hours or revenue.

#2954. Industry News: ‘We need more reviewers’: Finding Linux bugs is easy now – fixing them is another story

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (768 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: ‘We need more reviewers’: Finding Linux bugs is easy now – fixing them is another story

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (768 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that recently, Microsoft’s FORGE Lab reported that its AI scanning system, MDASH, turned up 59 upstream Linux kernel bug reports, including one flaw at least 21 years old.
  • Easy: in Linux, any bug can be a security bug.
  • In the latest Windows Patch Tuesday security release, Microsoft reported 726 CVEs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that recently, Microsoft’s FORGE Lab reported that its AI scanning system, MDASH, turned up 59 upstream Linux kernel bug reports, including one flaw at least 21 years old. That’s less impressive than it sounds. For 2026, through Nov. 2, the Linux Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) team reported an average of 27 CVEs a day.

Why so many? Easy: in Linux, any bug can be a security bug. As Linux Torvalds told me in 2024, “Bugs will happen, and anything can be a security bug if somebody is clever enough to just figure out how to abuse it.” Besides, since Linux runs everything from smartphones to refrigerators to supercomputers, what may be a serious bug in one device may not even appear at all on another.

It’s not just Linux, though. In the latest Windows Patch Tuesday security release, Microsoft reported 726 CVEs. The vast majority of these bug reports are coming from AI programmers. Finding bugs on anything is no longer the hard part. But reviewing and fixing them is, and both Microsoft developers and kernel maintainers are struggling to keep up.

Also: Microsoft fixes over 1,000 Windows flaws – and one is being exploited.

As the FORGE Lab mentioned, “Finding bugs and fixing them are drastically out of balance.” Turning its findings into reports took more than four person-months because “human effort [is] the bottleneck.”.

Recent findings suggest that that’s hurting the overworked maintainers. On Nov. 10, an ARM engineer and Linux kernel maintainer Lorenzo Stoakes gave up reviewing code. He’d been a reviewer for the memory-management core, misc, reclaim, and Rust-related sections. Stoakes, a kernel contributor since 2014,  wrote, “Given the current throughput in the kernel resulting from AI-generated series, I unfortunately lack the bandwidth to generally be able to offer review except in those areas I maintain.”.

Stoakes added, “Of course the AI wave has been horrible, and is getting significantly worse. At first it was once in a while that I’d see slop. Then it was at least once a week. Then every few days. Nowadays it’s pretty much half of what I see, if not more.”.

Also: Filing bugs for open-source apps is a huge help for devs – and easier than you think.

Recent findings suggest that he’s not alone. As Greg Kroah-Hartman, the Linux kernel stable maintainer, said in a Q&A session at Open Source Summit Europe, “We don’t have enough people to review them, the onslaught of the LLM-generated patches. We need more reviewers. We don’t have enough. All of the maintainers are burnt out, and we have been for ten years.”.

It’s not all doom and gloom, though. Linux Torvalds, Linux’s creator, mentioned in a recent Linux Kernel Mailing List (LKML) message that much of the new code in the Linux 7.4 rc 2 “was driven by various AI fixes.”.

Sources indicate that he continued, “that on the bpf [Berkeley Packet Filter]- side at least the fixes are now coming in faster than the latest reports, and that sounds lovely if true. I think most other areas haven’t reached that point yet, but it’s at least a sign that we _may_ be starting to see the tide starting to turn. Don’t hold your breath, but maybe cross your fingers we’ll be getting there in the not entirely distant future.”.

Recent findings suggest that we can but hope. In an interview, Kroah-Hartman isn’t so optimistic. “We are getting closer, yes, but not quite there yet.”  He’s not even willing to give a guesstimate of when human-approved AI fixes will catch up with and overcome AI bug reports.

Also: I locked down my OpenClaw agent with Claude Code – then dared it to escape.

Daniel Steinberg, the creator of the open-source cURL project, is also cautiously optimistic. Steinberg, who’s been especially critical of AI slop bug reports, told me in an interview that he now believes “we manage the flood pretty well so far, even if it goes a little up and down in periods depending exactly on who sends us a upcoming set of findings this particular week.”.

Still, while AI bugs remain a major headache for now, AI bug fixes, along with the work of thousands of maintainers, may finally be starting to stem the AI bug flood. I still foresee long days and nights of work ahead.

I also expect we’ll see more serious security breaches. In November alone, we saw a serious Linux TCP networking security hole revealed; the nasty Alpine Linux OpenSSH flaw; Alpine’s GitLab near-miss; and the wide-open PHP2Shell security problem, which many groups still haven’t patched.

#2951. Latest Update: I checked Gemini’s latest Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (669 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: I checked Gemini’s latest Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (669 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that like any AI, Google Gemini wants to remember things about you.
  • Also: I tried Claude Sheets on 3 tasks – and it saved me hours of work.
  • In a recent development, with a latest option called Memory summary, you’re able to view the details that Gemini has gathered about you over time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that like any AI, Google Gemini wants to remember things about you. The purported reason is to help tailor and personalize your conversations. But remember that your personal details may also wind up training the AI or even being reviewed by actual humans. With that in mind, you might want to find out just what Gemini knows about you. And now you can.

Also: I tried Claude Sheets on 3 tasks – and it saved me hours of work.

In a recent development, with a latest option called Memory summary, you’re able to view the details that Gemini has gathered about you over time. These may be tidbits from your conversations or things that you directly told the AI. Even better, you can add or remove any details just by editing the memory or issuing your request directly to Gemini.

This new capability is available in Gemini across the board, so you can access it at the Gemini website, in the mobile iOS and Android apps, and in the Windows and Mac desktop apps.

Industry observers note that launch Gemini via the web or in one of the mobile or desktop apps. In the left pane displaying your previous chats, select the Settings icon at the bottom. At the Settings screen, select Personal Intelligence and then click or tap Memory summary. If the option is grayed out, it means the Memory feature is turned off. To proceed, turn it back on. You can always turn if off again afterward if you wish.

Recent findings suggest that you’ll then see the individual details by category. My summary arranged the information across such categories as Essentials, Business & Career, Reading & Interests, and Culinary Preferences. Go down the list to see the individual items in each category. To view a recent history, tap the three dot-icon at the top and select Memory history. This shows you the latest changes and updates to Gemini’s memory.

Also: Stop sharing your passwords with AI agents.

What if Gemini’s memory includes details that are too personal or just incorrect? No problem. You can alter the AI’s memories of you. At the website or in one of the desktop apps, click the pencil icon at the top. Now you’re able to directly edit the text to add, remove, or revise specific details. After you’ve made your changes, just click Save.

Recent findings suggest that for example, my summary mentioned that I lived in Madison County. I have no idea where Gemini got that notion, as I live in New York. Here, I revised the text and saved the changes, which then synced across the Gemini website and apps.

In a recent development, the mobile apps have no direct editing capability. But there’s another method that works both on mobile and on the desktop. Just tell Gemini what change you want to make. At the prompt, type and speak your request, and the AI will carry it out for you.

Also: The best and worst AI for your privacy, ranked.

Industry observers note that as an example, my summary noted that I run a business called Batter Up selling collectible baseball cards. That’s not at all true. I had once referred to such a store only to test Gemini’s image creation skills to design a logo for a baseball card seller. Here, I simply told Gemini that I don’t run a business called Batter Up and asked it to remove that item from its memory. Poof, that detail swiftly disappeared.

Sources indicate that google isn’t exactly known as being privacy-friendly, and that extends to Gemini. In this case, though, I give the firm credit for offering this easy way to control the AI’s memories. I do find the memory feature useful as it recalls details about me that help personalize and direct its responses. But I don’t like Gemini or Google knowing too much about me. Now I can keep memory enabled and just control what it remembers about me.

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (765 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

AI finds zero-day flaws for just $4 now – even mediocre hackers can cash in

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (765 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the best AI models on the market couldn’t find zero-days earlier this year, but now they can in less than 15 minutes and at a cost of a few bucks, according to a new report from penetration testing firm Xint.io.
  • Every major AI developer is working at breakneck speed to improve model effectiveness.
  • This is good news for businesses trying to harness AI for productivity and upcoming services, but as token prices fall, it has also become cheaper for attackers to launch AI-assisted attacks, including software breaches caused by exploiting unknown vulnerabilities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the best AI models on the market couldn’t find zero-days earlier this year, but now they can in less than 15 minutes and at a cost of a few bucks, according to a new report from penetration testing firm Xint.io. The findings raise questions about how vulnerabilities will be discovered and exploited in the future.

Every major AI developer is working at breakneck speed to improve model effectiveness. At the same time, token prices continue to fall, with studies showing that the average cost of tokens, which varies by domain, has dropped by about 47% per quarter since 2023 and 15% last month alone, due to intense competition among companies including OpenAI and Anthropic.

This is good news for businesses trying to harness AI for productivity and upcoming services, but as token prices fall, it has also become cheaper for attackers to launch AI-assisted attacks, including software breaches caused by exploiting unknown vulnerabilities.

Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain.

Industry observers note that A report published by Xint.io examines how popular AI models have evolved over the past year to the point where cybersecurity tasks that would have failed only months ago now succeed. The team analyzed seven models launched since February 2026: two from OpenAI, three from Anthropic, and two open-source models from DeepSeek and Z.ai. The team tracked, over time, how they performed in finding a target vulnerability.

The target of this research was a security flaw in Google’s V8 engine. Tracked as CVE-2026-102321, the type confusion bug leading to remote code execution (RCE) was disclosed to the Google Vulnerability Reward Program (VRP) by Xint researcher Taisic Yun and so was not present in the AI models’ training datasets.

The research scope was limited to a set of source files, including the file containing the vulnerability, and each model was instructed to search for security problems within these files.

According to recent reports, xint’s first test was conducted in February. After 25 hours and $350 of scanning, the best models then available still couldn’t find the critical vulnerability.

In July, GPT 5.6 Sol found the zero-day flaw for $22 in 44 minutes.

Also: Finding Linux bugs is easy – fixing them is another story.

By September, GPT 6 Sol discovered the bug in 13 minutes for only $4.24 with its first guided prompt.

Only three of the seven models found the bug: GPT 6 Sol, GPT 5.6 Sol, and Claude Opus 5, all debuted from July onward. GPT 5.6 Sol needed two prompts, while Claude Opus 5 found it on its first try but at a higher cost of $43.40.

DeepSeek’s and Z.ai’s models failed the task.

The researchers say that the combination of AI model development and low token prices means that “mediocre hackers” can now use frontier models effectively to discover and potentially exploit vulnerabilities, and “while we are still far from complete amateurs using unharnessed models to hack systems and applications, what used to be considered too hard and costly to be worth the effort of the average hacker is now reachable.”.

As a result, organizations need to adjust their security posture accordingly — but falling token costs and evolving AI skills and speed can also work in your favor.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac.

In a recent development, there’s nothing stopping an organization’s security team or pentesters from running the same checks themselves to find vulnerabilities before threat actors do. AI-assisted tests, arguably, are no longer something that can be pushed back to next year’s budgetary review. By performing a risk assessment that focuses on likely weak spots, such as public-facing services or a digital supply chain that hasn’t been audited for years, organizations can mitigate the risk AI-enabled cyberattacks pose.

Zero-day vulnerabilities are unknown to vendors, and a patch might not be available when they go public or are actively exploited in the wild. So, AI can only go so far, but it can free up your defenders for tasks that need the human touch. Furthermore, maintaining zero-trust access controls, segmenting and shoring up your network’s defenses, and monitoring endpoints for signs of suspicious behavior can do as much as, or more than, AI.

As Xint notes, “expertise still matters” when it comes to instructing AI models to discover vulnerabilities. In some cases, the models couldn’t find the target vulnerability without guidance, so additional runs were needed, increasing time and cost.

“Software breaches still require some level of technical proficiency,” the researchers say, “but no longer top-of-the-distribution expertise.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in just a few years, businesses have adopted AI and large language models (LLMs) to manage everything from calendar invites to data analysis and programming. Bad actors steal credentials for those models through LLMjacking — and the marketplace is evolving.

Google’s latest report on AI threats, the Q4 AI Threat Tracker from the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG), found that gateways called LLM Mixers are selling access for cents on the dollar.

Also: 6 essential strategies to defend against AI-powered threat actors.

Industry observers note that organizations have poured billions of dollars into AI development and deployment, although the amount they spend on AI tokens every month varies. According to Ramp AI index data, among firms paying for AI, the top 1% spent over $10,000 per employee per month, compared with around $16 for the median firm. When employees have access to AI models, companies may introduce spending caps, but smaller outfits may overlook them.

LLMjacking is the theft of AI-related credentials, including usernames and passwords, or API keys, used to access AI models. This gives cybercriminals the opportunity to use tokens and AI resources belonging to a victim organization (or individual), typically with usage-based billing or subscriptions with no fixed cap.

With these credentials, an unauthorized user could run high-resource computing tasks, manage their own malicious AI deployments, extract and steal corporate data from the AI’s memory, or even poison training data. To add insult to injury, if demand outstrips the limits of the victim’s subscription, cybercriminals can rack up high usage costs that the victim is then on the hook for.

Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?

John Hultquist, chief analyst for GTIG, previously mentioned the cybersecurity unit has seen a “major increase” in LLMjacking over 2026, so we can assume this trend will likely continue into 2027 and beyond.

AI access is now a lucrative illegal business in its own right, leading to what Google calls LLM Mixers: “illicit storefronts” that provide unauthorized access to AI services and underlying proxy infrastructure.

After analyzing LLMJacking vendor advertisements on Russian- and Chinese-language marketplaces, GTIG researchers found that most offer access not only to frontier models from AI labs, but also to jailbroken models marketed as suitable for malicious purposes.

However, it doesn’t seem that many of these cybercriminal groups can agree on “reasonable” pricing, with prices swinging wildly depending on the models offered and the credentials available.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

Industry observers note that free trial credentials fetch far less than enterprise credentials, as you would expect. Token prices for business use ranged from $0.10 to $25, and one vendor, APIMart, increased its token price fivefold once a prompt exceeds 100,000 tokens. Other vendors offer subscription-based pricing.

Sources indicate that this might not seem like much at the lower tiers, but Sysdig estimates LLMJacking could cost around $46,000 based on earlier models, and even over $100,000 per day on cutting-edge models. Mandiant research published earlier this month recorded incidents with illicit AI usage exceeding $100,000 in only 24 hours, with cumulative charges at some organizations reaching $1 million before access was revoked.

While direct credentials can be sold, the infrastructure element is also an interesting service offering. Google’s threat team remarked in the report that the sale of LLM infrastructure “routes buyer traffic through a pool of stolen credentials and compute instances to ensure reliable access, while also offering the ability to spread query volume across multiple victim environments to reduce the likelihood of detection.”.

LLM Mixers look similar to the rest of the cybercriminal underground economy, in which traders tend to specialize in one or two parts of an attack chain. For example, an LLM Mixer offers the access and infrastructure needed to exploit an enterprise AI model, while its partners might break into victim networks to secure initial access or buy stolen credentials from operators of infostealer malware.

Avoid LLMjacking and having your organization’s AI added to a Mixer’s menu similarly to how you would prevent intrusions into SaaS applications and cloud setups: managing access, monitoring, and imposing restrictions.

Usage and spending are the first areas to tackle. By setting limits on how many tokens can be issued and used across every AI service and account, and by alerting when usage suddenly spikes, organizations can limit damage if an account is compromised and stop massive bills before they rack up.

Also: Can you still trust Proton?

Sources indicate that organizations should also try to prevent their keys from ending up in the hands of cyberattackers in the first place. Google recommends using a secrets manager that securely stores and frequently rotates API keys, and running audits to detect quiet probing, misconfigurations, or shadow accounts.

It’s also advisable, across the board, to implement phishing protections and multi-factor authentication (MFA) to make the business of stealing credentials or compromising your accounts and networks more difficult in the first place.

Lost or stolen Windows laptop? IT can lock it down without wiping it now

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft is testing a new feature that lets IT admins instantly lock down your lost or stolen device via remote connection, protecting your work projects and personal data from theft and unauthorized access.
  • Also: Windows 11 can run better on PCs with 8GB now.
  • The fresh remote lock feature is designed to work in tandem with other Microsoft services, such as Intune and BitLocker, to manage a fleet of devices both in-office and remotely across the globe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft is testing a new feature that lets IT admins instantly lock down your lost or stolen device via remote connection, protecting your work projects and personal data from theft and unauthorized access.

Also: Windows 11 can run better on PCs with 8GB now.

The fresh remote lock feature is designed to work in tandem with other Microsoft services, such as Intune and BitLocker, to manage a fleet of devices both in-office and remotely across the globe.

Once a device is reported missing or stolen, an admin can disable login access from anywhere without having to fully wipe the laptop or smartphone. Microsoft reports that the lockdown will persist across restarts, even if the device is disconnected from Wi-Fi networks, and can only be lifted by an admin. This means that thieves can’t use your passwords, PINs, or biometric data to circumvent the lock.

While the new feature allows IT admins to respond quickly when a laptop or phone is reported missing, there are still security gaps that other Windows controls must address. The new lock feature doesn’t erase your data or wipe your device if it can’t be recovered, nor does it isolate the missing device from corporate networks. Therefore, IT admins will still need to access those controls via the Intune and Microsoft Entra dashboards.

Also: You can now restore Windows 11 even if it can’t boot up.

Recent findings suggest that the remote lock feature also doesn’t change your Microsoft account credentials, so you can use your log-ins on other devices to recover your data, change passwords, and temporarily disable permissions. Finally, Remote lock doesn’t block the device from being booted in Safe Mode, from a USB, in Windows Recovery Mode, or if the storage drive is reimaged; Microsoft highly recommends keeping BitLocker enabled until the device can be wiped or recovered.

Microsoft blames major outage on a July enhancement defect – and two other factors

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft has released new information explaining the massive outage that started Thursday morning and affected Microsoft 365, Copilot, and Outlook access in 74 countries, according to Downdetector.
  • Sources indicate that charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents, and Platform, posted early Monday morning that the outage was due to three factors, including a “latent defect” from a July upgrade to Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers.
  • “A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft has released new information explaining the massive outage that started Thursday morning and affected Microsoft 365, Copilot, and Outlook access in 74 countries, according to Downdetector.

Sources indicate that charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents, and Platform, posted early Monday morning that the outage was due to three factors, including a “latent defect” from a July upgrade to Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. Low server capacity and peak traffic in the US brought the defect out of hiding, despite no prior reported concerns.

“A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions. This was due to lock contention inside an internal process which caused the machine to become unavailable,” Lamanna stated, noting that the update was deployed safely worldwide without any challenges for over three months.

He said Microsoft didn’t find the issue in testing due to “the different traffic and SKU mix used in our test labs,” because “our load testing tended to focus on our weaker hardware SKUs with fewer cores.”.

Also: Microsoft fixes over 1,000 Windows flaws – and one is being exploited.

Two other factors made matters worse, and left servers useless in less than two hours.

Recent findings suggest that “A surge in load increased the likelihood for the networking gateways to encounter the contention,” Lamanna noted, explaining that Microsoft 365 maintains two gateway systems. Before the outage started, Teams failed from one to the other, which “changed its traffic patterns.” Simultaneously, he added, “nearly 14% of server capacity for the networking gateway was out of service due to an unrelated issue from the previous day.”.

It has been revealed that those two conditions collided and “caused the network gateway to encounter the latent bug from July,” Lamanna concluded. Requests eventually overloaded servers, at which point they stopped responding. At the outage’s low point, over 80% of its servers weren’t responding.

Sources indicate that “When servers lose connectivity, our traffic management systems automatically route owners to other healthy endpoints,” Lamanna stated. “However, the redirected traffic increased the likelihood for the same problem to occur on the remaining endpoints. This caused a cascading failure from server to server as the same amount of load was spread across fewer servers.”.

Also: AI finds zero-day flaws for just $4 now – even mediocre hackers can cash in.

Before Microsoft issued an explanation, some suspected the outage may have been the result of a cyberattack, which both Lamanna and Microsoft’s status account denied.

Industry observers note that it’s unclear how many people the outage affected, though Microsoft’s own numbers from January say Microsoft 365 “exceeds 450 million commercial paid seats,” illustrating the scale of the glitch. Microsoft deployed an revision to fix the outage and gradually applied it to groups of servers. Lamanna said Microsoft would publish a full post-incident review with more details later this week.

Industry observers note that service might be restored, but customers aren’t happy about having lost nearly two full workdays. One think tank told CNN it estimated the outage — which lasted through close of business on Friday for some — resulted in $7 billion in losses, due to many businesses and organizations being unable to access their everyday systems.

Also: If the November Windows patch fails to install on your PC, here’s what to do.

The fact that Microsoft’s testing couldn’t find the July issue ahead of time may leave customers wondering when the next dormant defect will strike, and whether the company is prepared.

In a recent development, organizations across Europe have been leaving Microsoft in recent years, opting instead for locally-controlled, open-source alternatives. The former CEO of Github introduced a decentralized alternative called Entire earlier this year, citing developers’ need for something more reliable, as Github has similarly been plagued with outages.

For many, Teams was barely offline over the two-day period, or was the first service to come back online.

Recent findings suggest that “Several services like Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Office apps failed out of the faulty network gateway infrastructure. That is why those services were restored earlier, with Teams chats and meetings functioning without problem for most of the outage,” Lamanna explained. Other services like Exchange Online can’t fail out.

He added that fixing the outage was slow because waiting traffic hit servers as soon as they came back, rendering them unresponsive just as promptly.

In a recent development, “Our normally automated recovery processes were not designed to restore service from this broad unresponsive state,” Lamanna noted. “Additionally, since the main code defect was a latent bug from several months previous, our normal rollback, flighting, and feature flags were unable to promptly revert the change.”.

On Thursday morning, people began reporting complications with Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, according to Downdetector. By 1 p.m. ET, the number of reported Outlook outages was nearly 83,000 but had fallen to just under 75,000 by 2:38 p.m. ET. Teams and Copilot reports started dropping significantly by Thursday evening, but many individuals were still reporting issues accessing systems well into Friday morning on X and Reddit. Even Microsoft’s status page was down until around 3 p.m. ET Thursday.

Also: If the November Windows revision fails to install on your PC, here’s what to do.

As late as Friday afternoon, the manufacturer didn’t yet have an ETA of when the outage would be fully solved.

Google has made it easy to build step-by-step itineraries and get real-time route details when you pull up directions. You can use Ask Maps to blueprint simple tasks, like a day of holiday shopping, or more complex plans, like a multi-day road trip with stops along the way.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, samsung’s Galaxy AI may be getting a cross-app intelligence upgrade, à la Google’s Gemini Intelligence and Apple’s Siri AI, according to an Android Authority report. Samsung is working on Galaxy Claw, which could make Galaxy AI more agentic and context-aware across your apps.

Also: Samsung mulls Galaxy AI usage limits and subscription tiers.

Right now, Galaxy AI lives inside your Galaxy devices and apps, but its smarts are limited to the apps it’s integrated with. Android Authority reports that Samsung’s Personal Agent Core is at the center of Galaxy Claw, connecting Galaxy AI to compatible apps and services, such as Calendar, Contacts, Messages, Gmail, Gallery, Phone, and Voice Recorder.

Android Authority found code that referred to Galaxy Claw in Samsung’s Personal Agent Core app, suggesting that Galaxy AI can complete cross-app tasks. For example, take the request: “Remind me to buy Mom a birthday card two days before her birthday.” An assistant without access to multiple apps will set a reminder to buy Mom a birthday card, but you might have to manually enter the date and time for the reminder to notify you.

Industry observers note that with a more agentic assistant, it can access Mom’s contact card and her birthdate, calculate two days before her birthday, and remind you on that date. Like Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI, Personal Agent Core will need special permissions to access your sensitive information, such as messages, photos, and calls.

Also: 4 ways Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Android Authority also reports that code strings in the app point to a recurring, scheduled tasks feature, which would allow consumers to create custom automations and determine how often Galaxy AI should execute them, similar to Apple’s revamped Shortcuts.

Other code strings reveal a Daily Brief, Device Cleaner, Travel Planner, and a widget. An AI-powered daily brief is something I’ve been yearning for as an iPhone user. If I want a Siri-created brief, I’d have to build it via Shortcuts.

Gmail features a Gemini-powered daily brief, which compiles information from my email inbox and GChat messages to show me things I may have missed. I find it very useful for work, since my inbox is flooded and I often miss key emails.

Also: I’m a ChatGPT power user, but I won’t give it my wallet.

Samsung’s Galaxy ecosystem includes smartphones, smartwatches, smart rings, earbuds, and tablets, so there are plenty of opportunities for a more agentic Galaxy AI to bridge gaps across the devices in your personal ecosystem.

Additionally, Google Gemini integration is sweeping across Android (and iOS) apps, which might prompt Galaxy owners to choose the more robust AI assistant over Galaxy AI. If Samsung can find ways to make Galaxy AI more useful and exclusive to Galaxy users, it might win some people over. However, reports say Samsung is testing subscriptions for heavy Galaxy AI users, so more Galaxy AI integration might incur a fee.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Meta will let creators decide to hide copies of their videos flagged by a latest ‘content protection’ feature.
  • Meta will let creators decide to hide copies of their videos flagged by a upcoming ‘content protection’ feature.
  • Instagram is beginning to roll out a “content protection” feature that lets creators see and review copies of their videos posted to the platform.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta will let creators decide to hide copies of their videos flagged by a latest ‘content protection’ feature.

Meta will let creators decide to hide copies of their videos flagged by a upcoming ‘content protection’ feature.

Instagram is beginning to roll out a “content protection” feature that lets creators see and review copies of their videos posted to the platform.

Recent findings suggest that “For eligible creators who enroll, content protection is a tool that automatically looks out for visual matches of your original videos, alerts you when we find a match across Instagram and Facebook, and lets you decide what happens next,” Meta says in a blog post. Meta launched a similar tool for Facebook last year to help customers “safeguard” their Reels and “maintain control” over their creative work.

When an Instagram creator is notified of a matched video, they can see how many views the match has and decide if they want to track the video, hide it from everyone on Instagram and Facebook, add a credit link, or release their claim on the match.

After a creator enrolls, every “original video” they post on Instagram is protected, and creators can retroactively protect older videos manually. Creators can also put accounts on an allow list that lets them use their videos.

In addition, Instagram will start flagging AI-generated videos that “match the spoken words” in a creator’s original video but have visuals replaced with AI. Initially, Instagram will test this with a “small group of creators” in “the coming weeks.” The platform notes it’s exploring ways to limit the reach of content and profiles that “use AI tools to post this type of content repeatedly.”.
