Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

iPhone Duo 2 prototypes suggest Face ID, Action Button, other potential 2027 features

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (665 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that although the iPhone Duo was released just this fall, Apple is finalizing the foldable’s second generation.
  • Apple reportedly wants to bring Face ID to the foldable, potentially integrating it into the outer display.
  • Also: iPhone Duo review: Hard to recommend, even harder to put down.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that although the iPhone Duo was released just this fall, Apple is finalizing the foldable’s second generation. According to a Bloomberg report, Apple has already created prototypes for the second iPhone Duo, codenamed V78, and some include a sought-after feature: Face ID.

Apple reportedly wants to bring Face ID to the foldable, potentially integrating it into the outer display. However, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman notes that Apple appears to be running out of time to finalize its looks for the Duo ahead of a fall 2027 launch.

Also: iPhone Duo review: Hard to recommend, even harder to put down.

According to recent reports, iPhone launch events typically take place in early September, when Apple releases its new smartphone lineups. To have the iPhones ready for sale on the heels of their announcement, Apple must manufacture the new models well before the launch event.

Because of this timeline concern, Face ID isn’t guaranteed for the iPhone Duo 2, though it could come to a third generation instead.

Other planned uogrades — including an Action Button, a telephoto camera, and a thinner, lighter construction — are also noted in the report.

Apple reportedly wants to add an Action Button, the customizable button that performs an action when pressed. The iPhone Duo 2 may combine the Action Button and the Camera Control buttons into a single button, providing a useful physical shortcut instead of adding a new button.

Sources indicate that the report indicates that many customers don’t use the camera control button as often as Apple expected. Combining the camera and action buttons gives Apple the real estate necessary to add both options in an already constrained space.

Recent findings suggest that apple also wants to incorporate a telephoto camera into the iPhone Duo, though this is likely to happen in one of the next couple of generations. A telephoto camera would give users greater flexibility to zoom in and capture clear photos of distant objects, which would be an upgrade to the Duo’s photography features.

Recent findings suggest that technically, equipping the Duo with a telephoto camera is feasible, but the biggest obstacle is space constraints. A telephoto camera needs more room than a wide-angle one, since it requires additional optical elements to magnify distant objects.

Apple already uses a tetraprism design in its Pro iPhones, which allows a longer optical path without too much physical depth.

Apple also wants to reduce the weight and thickness of the iPhone Duo, which is legitimately clunky and cumbersome. To do this, Apple needs to balance the large internal and outer displays, battery capacity, camera array, and the hinge mechanism.

Also: The iPhone Action Button you’re hardly using has a superpower.

For many people, reducing the weight and thickness of a passport-sized foldable could matter more in buying decisions than adding another button or camera.

Gurman’s latest report doesn’t mention any planned changes for the iPhone Duo’s hinge mechanism, even after concerns with the first generation’s durability. With manufacturing deadlines fast approaching, however, it’s unlikely that Apple will be able to make changes to the Duo 2 based on consumer feedback. More than likely, these changes would come with the third-generation model.

In a recent development, CNET tested the iPhone Duo’s hinge mechanism and found that, after around 440,000 cycles, the hinge stopped opening flat on its own. Loosening and other signs of wear were evident after 390,000 folds.

Also: The best iPhone Duo cases: Expert recommended.

Given the thinner, lighter construction of a future Duo model, one could assume that changes to the hinge and the foldable’s internal structure are imminent, but this has not been confirmed.

Because Apple will not have enough time to gather feedback on the iPhone Duo before the manufacturing deadlines for the iPhone Duo 2, I don’t expect the second-generation iPhone Duo to be significantly different from its predecessor. We do expect a thinner iPhone Duo 2 and a way to incorporate the Action and Camera buttons.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, meta’s chief AI officer posted an AI video of a top competitor.
  • Meta’s chief AI officer posted an AI video of a top competitor.
  • Instagram is filled with people posting deepfaked content — including, as of late, from one of Meta’s most prominent executives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, meta’s chief AI officer posted an AI video of a top competitor. It’s allowed under Meta’s AI policy.﻿.

Meta’s chief AI officer posted an AI video of a top competitor. It’s allowed under Meta’s AI policy.﻿.

Instagram is filled with people posting deepfaked content — including, as of late, from one of Meta’s most prominent executives.

It has been revealed that earlier in November, Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, shared a short clip to promote Muse, the company’s consumer AI agent. In the AI-generated clip, Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Jolly, the anthropomorphic mascot of Muse, are on a four-way video call. When Altman joins the call he’s dressed like Jolly, wearing a furry hooded suit and face paint to look like the cutesy character. The clip is captioned “When the homies meet about openai product strategy,” a reference to the AI agent race and the recent popularity of Muse.

Industry observers note that just a few years ago, AI content portraying real people led to strong public statements rebuking the use of the technology to imitate humans. In some cases legal action was threatened. Now, AI content has become part of the texture of a new reality, especially on social media. Leading up to the midterm elections, for example, political groups ran millions of dollars’ worth of AI-generated ads attacking opponents.

Wang has been doing a lot of what some have described as “anti-PR” to promote Muse, tweeting hundreds of times and referring to more traditional marketers as “corposlops.” Still, a major tech executive posting an AI video of a competitor is notable, especially on a platform that’s been criticized recently over AI-generated content. After an AI-generated image of actress Mia Goth gained traction in October, the Pearl star’s representative told The Verge it was “incomprehensible” that Instagram allowed the image to spread instead of focusing on the “protection and integrity of a public figure’s likeness.” Other celebrities, including Scarlett Johansson, are regularly the subject of sexualized AI imagery; Meta has removed some accounts in the past that it found to be posing as someone else and using their likeness.

Industry observers note that meta requires AI-generated videos depicting people to be labeled as AI, like Wang’s post is. Static images, however, have no such requirement, meaning the AI image of Goth had no disclosure. To make matters worse, the image was shared by a fan account with a blue verification badge given by Instagram.

Sources indicate that reached for comment, Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton noted that Wang’s post is labeled as AI content. Clayton also pointed out that Altman has made his likeness available for AI content generation, as when OpenAI introduced its Sora app (and it was quickly flooded with fake Altman videos). OpenAI didn’t respond to requests for comment.

#2929. Latest Update: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1178 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1178 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities.
  • Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?
  • Industry observers note that the capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities. According to Google, this is now happening at scale.

Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?

Industry observers note that the capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate. Like it or not, AI has an integral role in the fresh reality — for the defenders and threat actors.

Speed and scale are the main reasons enterprises consider adopting AI in SOCs and for security more broadly, and these factors underpin Google’s newly introduced security forecast for 2027 — Cloud CISO Perspectives. However, without the right precautions, AI security adopters could inadvertently increase their attack surface rather than shrink it.

With this in mind, these are five ways AI will change the security industry over the next year and what CISOs need to consider going into 2027.

Alert fatigue is well-known across SOC teams. Alert after alert needs to be trawled through; many are irrelevant or false positives, tying up skilled staff with the mundane, tedious, time-consuming task of triaging them.

Now that autonomous, AI-driven threats can probe a network, gain entry, and move laterally across it in minutes, chasing threat data and security alerts from multiple systems logged days or weeks ago can’t help a business mitigate them — and certainly not at the speed of the threat.

Industry observers note that according to Google’s forecast, AI will mean the alert queue quietly disappears. Ramya Chitrakar, VP of engineering at Google Cloud Security, believes that “2027 is the year analysts stop chasing alerts and start shaping outcomes.”.

Also: AI is both a cyber weapon and a massive target.

According to recent reports, how? CISOs must change the alert model itself. Instead of human defenders triaging alerts at the start of a cybersecurity incident, the alert becomes final output, with autonomous agents handling “data enrichment, correlation, and triage automatically, surfacing a verified conclusion rather than a raw ticket,” according to Google.

This means cybersecurity experts can oversee alert handling and verify automated actions, potentially freeing them to focus on other tasks.

Industry observers note that custom agentic AI is often designed — or at least intended — to work autonomously, with human oversight. However, having thousands of individual agents working across multiple environments can create high-value entry points into corporate networks that cyberattackers target.

We need to think of agentic AI as more than a tool: each one needs its own identity, like a human employee, to operate within a zero-trust architecture, retain control, and reduce the risk of compromise.

Also: Your enterprise AI access can be sold for pennies – beware ‘LLM Mixers’.

However, Heather Adkins, VP of security engineering at Google, thinks this needs to go further and suggests the zero-trust concept shouldn’t stop at the network layer. Instead, Adkins believes it needs to reach the transaction layer.

Sources indicate that A paper trail for each agent needs to be established, which is impossible to handle manually, and even within a zero-trust framework, AI agents could be given too much scope. Instead, implement verification for each transaction and for every authorization, and assign each AI agent its own least-privilege set of credentials that can be revoked if there is a security incident or the agent is no longer required.

“When backed by real-time autonomous reasoning, we can dynamically allow a transaction on Tuesday and block the exact same request on Wednesday if conditions look anomalous,” the report notes.

AI is being used to speed up the development and deployment of latest software, and in 2027, security will have to become a continuous system embedded in the software delivery pipeline, according to Google.

Recent findings suggest that threat actors have carried out software supply chain attacks over the years, one of the most notable being the SolarWinds incident of 2020. Sandra Joyce, VP of Google Threat Intelligence, notes cybercriminals are now poisoning everything from open-source code to software libraries, which AI coding assistants often pull automatically into codebases.

Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain.

Recent findings suggest that bug-fix tickets that take days to respond to and security appearing at the end of a software development cycle no longer work. Instead, writing and securing code must happen simultaneously, with the help of agentic AI, so speed doesn’t compromise security.

“It’s also crucial that we link live production environments directly back to source code so that defenders can trace a real-world exposure to the exact line of code, validate whether it is genuinely exploitable, and deliver a pre-tested fix at machine speed without breaking production,” Google added.

As organizations rush to implement AI into their applications and services to appear “AI-first,” innovative, and modern, security may be ignored or treated as an afterthought.

As a result, we may face a newly introduced, broader attack surface than we realize, as AI introduces new security complications, including software vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, bypasses, and indirect prompt injection attacks. Now that AI is also in the hands of all cyberattackers — from script kiddies to state-sponsored groups — auditing corporate networks and infrastructure is crucial.

Industry observers note that also: Who’s responsible for catching rogue AI agents? You are.

It has been revealed that penetration testing and red team exercises now need to cover agentic AI. This wasn’t in scope for many red teams only a few years ago, but now that businesses have run with the idea of implementing AI in their workflows, processes, and products, organizations need to identify and fix security challenges introduced by AI before threat actors take advantage of them.

CISOs should task pen testers with auditing before an autonomous workflow hits production, then combine the results with threat intelligence to ensure defenders have the information they need to bolster network defenses and harden classifiers against latest and novel attacks.

The final significant trend we are likely to see in 2027 is tackling agent sprawl to create coordinated teams of AI agents that can rapidly handle security tasks at scale.

Single AI agents given general instructions won’t cut it when AI-assisted attackers can compromise endpoint devices, enter networks, move laterally, or start stealing data in a far shorter timeframe than before. Instead, CISOs should replace these “generalist” AI agents with specialized, orchestrated teams of AI agents that can meet the demands of defending against AI-driven attacks by employing specialist tooling and skill sets.

Also: AI agent kill switch urged by Okta-led alliance.

According to recent reports, CISOs also need to ensure that each agent has its own domain training and understanding, memory, and dedicated tools, and can act on its own within set limits, with a central coordinator that knows when to hand a decision to a human. This requires oversight, but in return, organizations will avoid agent sprawl, which the tech giant believes is the next iteration of shadow IT and its associated threats.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The first shoes with Nike’s new Tuned Air technology will be available for runners starting in late 2027.﻿.
  • In 2024, Nike confirmed its Air Max 1000 that were manufactured using a 3D-printing process resulting in a shoe that had a uniform silhouette but varying areas of support and flexibility throughout.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first shoes with Nike’s new Tuned Air technology will be available for runners starting in late 2027.﻿.

The first shoes with Nike’s new Tuned Air technology will be available for runners starting in late 2027.﻿.

In 2024, Nike confirmed its Air Max 1000 that were manufactured using a 3D-printing process resulting in a shoe that had a uniform silhouette but varying areas of support and flexibility throughout. The company is now doing something similar with its iconic air-filled soles using its new Tuned Air technology. While previously the level of cushioning in Nike Air shoes was uniform across the entire sole, a new manufacturing process can produce multiple air pockets with varying levels of cushioning and stability.

Sources indicate that nike has been putting air pockets into its shoes for nearly 50 years as a way to increase comfort and cushioning while making them lighter. Its air pockets have even found their way into apparel as a way to improve insulation by trapping body heat, but Nike plans to use its fresh Tuned Air technology as a way to customize the cushioning experience in its shoes and tailor them to specific athletes and sports. The first shoes featuring the technology are expected to arrive in late 2027 and will be targeted at runners.

Sources indicate that while one of Nike’s earliest successes was track shoes with a grip design inspired by a waffle iron, the manufacturer credits the “vibrant colors on magazine covers” as the inspiration for its latest shoe technology. A Tuned Air sole is manufactured using a “proprietary digital print and selective lamination process” where an ink is applied in specific patterns that define where the layers bond to each other. This process can be used to create internal pockets in an unlimited combination of shapes and sizes, and by fine-tuning how much air is in each of those pockets, some parts of the sole can feel firmer while others feel softer.

Recent findings suggest that the Tuned Air technology will not only allow Nike to highly customize the fit and feel of air sole shoes for different sports, it will also help keep the benefits of the custom tuning consistent across different sizes. The upcoming manufacturing process will also help reduce the amount of time it takes Nike to go from a concept for a new shoe to a final design ready for production. “Prototypes that once took three weeks can now be made in three days,” the organization claims in a release today. That gives Nike’s designers more time to refine new shoes, and more opportunity to experiment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia’s Q3 revenue has more than doubled, with income from data centers up 110 percent from last year, to $107.6 billion.

Nvidia’s Q3 revenue has more than doubled, with income from data centers up 110 percent from last year, to $107.6 billion.

It has been revealed that interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress announced the organization’s Q3 earnings on Tuesday, without initially mentioning former CEO Jensen Huang or the details of his departure, or possible attempt at a return. On the earnings call accompanying the release, board chair Harvey Jones kicked things off by saying the board “does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO,” and that “we will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation,” before Kress started with her comments on the results.

Sources indicate that as it predicted in the last financial update, Nvidia is now on the list of companies that have pulled in over $100 billion in a single quarter, with revenues of $115.8 billion, up 103 percent from the same period last year and higher than its expectation of $108 billion. This quarter’s figures include data center revenues of $107.6 billion, which were up 110 percent, and edge computing (which includes the consumer gaming PC business and devices like the new RTX Spark laptops) revenue of $8.2 billion, up 42 percent.

The organization reported $65.3 billion in profit, a new record.

“Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” said Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.”.

In the fourth quarter, Nvidia expects revenues of $130 billion.

Revision, November 17th: Added comments from Nvidia’s earnings call.

😱 Crypto Hits Extreme Fear as Bitcoin Plunges.

The Crypto Fear and Greed Index printed 10 on Sunday. A month ago it read 63, which is Greed. A week ago it was 28. It has been sliding every day since, and 10 is about as low as that gauge goes.

This weekend’s price action certainly was extremely fearful. Bitcoin touched roughly $62,000 before stabilizing in the mid-60s, down about a quarter from its early-October high and down something like 9% in three days. ETH fell under $1,850. Solana, XRP and dogecoin are all down more than 25% on the month. Bitcoin is now trading below its 200-week moving average, a level that has historically acted as the floor beneath every cycle, and it lost its 50-week average a week earlier.

It wasn’t just majors. Zcash fell to $800. Hype fell to $62. VVV went sub-$17. Nothing was spared.

The billion-dollar question of course—why is Bitcoin (and crypto) selling off so hard?

CZ addressed the question directly on Sunday, saying “No one knows for sure. Correlation does not prove causation.” But he did give potential reasons.

No one knows for sure. Correlation does not prove causation. Here are some potential reasons.

Money shifting to the Anthropic IPO: https://t.co/jYwVi4huAY.

ETF outflows: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about $1.9 billion in outflows over seven trading… pic.twitter.com/XL2aB1ZL9W.

Industry observers note that those are all pretty valid. Some of those overhangs remove soon (Anthropic IPO), some will fade over time (political uncertainty), but the cyber attack threat will remain until Bitcoin and broader crypto can present a real solution. And if we are faced with a hiking cycle in 2027 due to inflation, that will certainly be a continued headwind.

Industry observers note that so where does this leave us? Nvidia reports Tuesday with an interim CEO while its former one openly campaigns to return. The Fed meets December 9 with inflation running hot enough to put another hike in play. And Bitcoin is sitting under a technical level that has held for three cycles.

Extreme fear has marked bottoms before. It has also marked the middle of declines. Now we wait for something other than sentiment to turn.

Nvidia notes it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The board said it would not take additional questions on the call about Huang’s departure.
  • The board mentioned it would not take additional questions on the call about Huang’s departure.
  • Starting Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, new board chair Harvey Jones said that when former CEO Jensen Huang resigned, “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The board said it would not take additional questions on the call about Huang’s departure.

The board mentioned it would not take additional questions on the call about Huang’s departure.

Starting Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, new board chair Harvey Jones said that when former CEO Jensen Huang resigned, “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”.

Jones added, “We will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation.”.

Huang had publicly floated the idea of returning earlier on Tuesday. In a statement posted to X, he wrote that he “did not live up to the standards expected of everyone” at the organization, that he regretted his mistakes, and that he would cooperate with the Nvidia board’s investigation into his actions. He added that he’d be willing to return to the chief executive role if offered it, though a day earlier, the Nvidia board reportedly said it was not considering bringing him back. “NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company,” Huang wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”.

Industry observers note that but since his November 12th resignation, Huang remains entangled in scandal. He’s reportedly had three affairs, two with subordinates at Nvidia, one with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset suspected of facilitating illicit chip sales. (Huang has pushed against restrictions on Nvidia chip sales in China.) He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st, and an internal company investigation is ongoing.

It has been revealed that tech industry heavyweights have still voiced their support for Huang, dubbing him “irreplaceable” and petitioning for his return. Some have cast doubt on the allegations that Alice Huang (no relation) was spying on behalf of China and painted the leaks about their relationship as a conspiracy against the former CEO. President Donald Trump, a close ally of Huang for much of the past year, has also backed him. On Monday, Trump mentioned he “would not mind” Huang returning, adding that “I think he learned a significant lesson — I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another.”.

Trump’s closeness with Huang could also complicate things for Nvidia, however. The company has ramped up its lobbying in Washington, D.C., spending $5 million in 2025 and $4.7 million so far in 2026. But as Democrats prepare to take Congress, they’re planning to investigate Trump’s dealings with Big Tech and other industries, alleging potential corruption. “The election wasn’t very positive for AI, and [the news around Huang’s resignation] is only going to complicate things, especially for the company in particular but for AI as a whole going forward,” Brendan Glavin, director of insights at OpenSecrets, told The Verge in an interview last week.

Lior Prosor, managing partner at Deep33, a tech VC firm, said last week that he didn’t expect Huang’s resignation to pop the AI bubble, although Huang has had a significant hand in mobilizing funds for the AI infrastructure buildout in the U.S. Under Huang’s leadership in August, Nvidia entered into partnerships with six financial institutions for about $500 billion to fund such endeavors. “NVIDIA supplies roughly 75 percent of the AI compute hardware the industry consumes, and demand continues to dramatically outpace supply,” Deep33’s Prosor said in an interview with The Verge. “Neither its customers nor its competitors can easily replace the capabilities it provides, and the economic incentives driving the AI trade remain unchanged.”.

Even so, a potential market cooling has some worried, as Anthropic’s IPO, slated to potentially be the largest of all time, is set for Thursday. The chipmaker had agreed to buy $10 billion in Anthropic shares via private placement, on top of a $10 billion funding promise Nvidia had already made last year.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, apple is exploring how people use AI for their health, presumably to build its own AI health coach. On Sunday, it released the Apple Health AI Usage Study, which could contribute to the next AI health experience Apple builds by measuring the quality of AI health responses, comprehension, and everyday health behaviors, according to a press release.

According to recent reports, apple is conducting the study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform widely used by healthcare professionals. The study examines the relationship between conversational AI tools, like chatbots, and the people who use them.

“Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, remarked in the press release.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

Sources indicate that participants are encouraged to share their HealthKit data and query the health app with questions. The study will also explore how AI tools can best prepare patients ahead of clinical visits. Apple will monitor the AI’s clarity and approachability when providing medical information, and each response or recommendation will be linked to peer-reviewed clinical citations. Responses could be unclear or incomplete, which is why Apple is rolling this out as a study to explore a responsibly designed AI health assistant.

In a recent development, apple often launches studies for features it would like to develop in the future. For example, many of the hearing health features released on the AirPods were a direct result of the findings from Apple’s Hearing Study.

Also: Athenahealth patients can ask Claude about their medical records now.

According to recent reports, the AI usage study comes on the heels of the revamped Health app’s debut, which launches officially next month. It also arrives amid a bevy of AI health coaches, popping up alongside companion health devices. Google introduced its AI Health Coach in Google Health Premium last year, and Oura launched a proprietary AI model for women trained on medical standards and research from Oura’s in-house team of board-certified clinicians.

A growing number of Americans are relying on AI for medical advice. A recent survey from Pew Research Center found that 34% of US adults have talked with a chatbot for medical advice. As AI proliferates, that percentage will only increase.

Industry observers note that “Patients and clinicians are both turning to AI, but the tools they use are being built and tested in separate worlds,” stated Robert M. Wachter, M.D., UCSF’s professor and chair of the Department of Medicine, in the press release.

Apple and other tech companies are building for this latest health normal, and the AI usage study indicates that Apple isn’t taking the responsibility lightly.

If you’re interested in participating in Apple’s study, it’s open to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older in the US. You’ll need a phone with Apple Intelligence enabled (the iPhone 15 Pro or later), running iOS 26 or later. You can download the study app to learn more and enroll.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Apple’s inroads on designing repairable devices seems to have been abandoned with the HomeView.﻿.
  • After finding recent versions of Apple’s iPads and HomePods much easier to disassemble for battery replacements or other repairs, iFixit assumed it would be the same story for Apple’s upcoming HomeView hub that looks like a seven-inch tablet stuck to a smart speaker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s inroads on designing repairable devices seems to have been abandoned with the HomeView.﻿.

Apple’s inroads on designing repairable devices seems to have been abandoned with the HomeView.﻿.

After finding recent versions of Apple’s iPads and HomePods much easier to disassemble for battery replacements or other repairs, iFixit assumed it would be the same story for Apple’s upcoming HomeView hub that looks like a seven-inch tablet stuck to a smart speaker. The reality was much different and by the time they got the HomeView apart iFixit’s skilled techs had “ripped a connector, snapped a speaker in two, and put more force on the poor logic board than any of us were comfortable with.”.

It has been revealed that the tablet section of the HomeView proved to be the bigger challenge to disassemble as a result of some questionable decisions with Apple’s design. The glue used to secure the display in place “held on harder than on any Apple product we’ve opened recently,” iFixit says. And while Apple’s decision to turn the HomeView’s entire aluminum chassis into a heat sink was clever, the thermal bond between a heat shield and the device’s logic board made separating the two a “remarkably risky operation.” While these design decisions possibly streamlined assembly at a factory, the extensive use of glue makes servicing the HomeView incredibly difficult.

In an accompanying teardown video iFixit also reveals how much smaller the speaker drivers are in the wall-mounted version of the HomeView versus the tabletop option. Although both versions are priced at $299, the wall version costs a little more when you factor in the required mount that’s not included, leaving iFixit feeling that you’re getting less performance while spending more money.

Harvey C. Jones said the company would not be addressing or taking questions ‘regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation.’﻿.

Sources indicate that nvidia’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday was its first with CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress at the helm alongside the company’s first board chair, Harvey C. Jones. The leadership change followed Jensen Huang’s resignation last week after reports he had multiple affairs – including one with former Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese asset Alice Huang and one with a direct report, Kimberly Powell. Nvidia is investigating whether Huang’s relationship with the former compromised national security or company secrets. Huang will also testify before lawmakers on December 1st.

Ahead of Tuesday’s earnings, Huang said he would be willing to return as CEO. However, during the company’s earnings call, Jones stated that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted [Huang’s] resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Jones also said that during the call, the company would not be addressing or taking questions “regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation.” He added that, “the Board is proactively dealing with the immediate consequences facing the company, as well as enhancing our oversight capacity going forward.”.

In Tuesday’s earnings Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, continuing years of skyrocketing revenue driven by the AI industry.

Jones shared the following enhancement on the company:.

Recent findings suggest that as Chairman of NVIDIA’s Board of Directors, I want to say a few words on the Board’s behalf. NVIDIA is an exceptionally strong company. Its strength comes from its extraordinary people, groundbreaking technology, and exemplary track record of execution. Our financial performance speaks for itself.

On November 12th, our Board of Directors unveiled that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as President, CEO, and board member. The NVIDIA Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO. The Board appointed Colette Kress, NVIDIA’s longtime and well-respected CFO, as interim CEO. In addition, the Board announced it was initiating a search for a permanent chief executive, and we have since retained Heidrick and Struggles to lead the search.

While this was an unexpected transition, the Board acted deliberately and in the best interest of the tech giant’s employees, customers, partners, and shareholders. This morning, the company revealed that our Board has established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee that will include a select group of our independent Board directors, senior external advisors, and legal counsel.

According to recent reports, this committee will enhance— will– excuse me, will enhance our engagement with the U.S. government, including all relevant agencies. We will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation. Our Board will communicate further when appropriate. On behalf of our shareholders, the Board is proactively dealing with the immediate consequences facing the tech giant, as well as enhancing our oversight capacity going forward.

We have an incredibly talented leadership team, and we have every confidence in Colette’s leadership, integrity, and ability to deliver as interim CEO. Colette has been at the center of this firm’s extraordinary growth for the last— growth for the last 13 years, instrumental in executing strategy, and with a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations, and financial position. The Board and the entire leadership team remain laser-focused on driving NVIDIA forward. Our commitment to generating value for shareholders, customers, and partners remains unchanged.

Kress responded to a question about the company’s leadership transition, saying “the most vital thing that we think through right now is our employees.” She added, “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual.”.

Jones also gave an update on Nvidia’s search for a fresh permanent CEO:.

Industry observers note that from the board’s point of view, we take the search very seriously. We’re going to look into internal candidates as well as external candidates. The Board appreciates that we’re living in a world where the advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are making major changes in our marketplace. Our newly introduced CEO will have to navigate those waters very carefully. So, the search will be thorough and we want to install the CEO, the permanent CEO, as rapidly as possible, but we won’t expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person.

Robert Pattinson’s casting as James Bond made enough sense given his recent work with director Denis Villeneuve, who’s making the franchise’s next film over at Amazon. But it turns out that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos played a significant role in making the final decision, too.

During Semafor’s Silicon Valley and the World conference today, Bezos said that he was “heavily involved” in the process of casting the newest 007:.

We ran a really tight process and we made the final decision on Friday. There was a massive group initially, and we down-selected to five finalists. Then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists, and it was really interesting — full costume, real sets, other actors. We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists, and then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all those screening tests, and reviewing all of that. And all of the actors were extraordinarily talented.

Recent findings suggest that by the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing, but there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances. It was kind of immediately undebated. Denis — the director — we all sort of gravitated to Rob. By the way, initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him, just because he’s already so famous. We sort of thought, ‘maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown.’  But in the screen test, it was so obvious. He is James Bond.

Sources indicate that it’s not exactly surprising that a studio leader would want to have a say in casting the newly introduced face for one of their most lucrative franchises. But with Bezos being so hands-on, one can only image what this new era of Bond films will look and feel like once Amazon starts releasing them in theaters.

The number-one pick among ZDNET readers is sadly no longer in production. More: Why I’m recommending the Sony Bravia 8 II over competing OLED TVs – especially to enthusiasts.

Most Accurate HDR Color Reproduction.

Industry observers note that the Hisense U7 splits the difference between premium and midrange, offering crisp 4K resolution, bold colors, and rich sound. You can also share media from your iOS and Android devices via both AirPlay and Google Cast.

It has been revealed that samsung’s OLED TV options have continuously topped our lists as some of the best TVs you can buy almost since the minute they hit the market. And the S95F is no exception, even though it’s last year’s flagship. With a peak brightness of 5,000 nits, you’ll get excellent visibility in almost any lighting environment — even direct sunlight — while the 5,000 local dimming zones give you OLED-level contrast for sharper image quality.

The QM8 has a base refresh rate of 120Hz that can be boosted to 144Hz for console gaming, while AMD FreeSync Premium Pro VRR support prevents stuttering and freezing while gaming. The TCL QM8 is available in sizes up to 115 inches, but ZDNET readers most often opt for the 65-, 85-, and 98-inch models for both typical living rooms and dedicated home theaters.

6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly improve my browsing experience

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (777 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, whether you’re a longtime Chrome user or just now switching to Google’s browser, you might assume that Chrome is perfectly fine right out of the box.
  • But Chrome’s default settings could use some improvement (as is the case with most software).
  • The single most important thing you can do in any browser is to enable the best protection it offers for your needs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, whether you’re a longtime Chrome user or just now switching to Google’s browser, you might assume that Chrome is perfectly fine right out of the box. That’s understandable, given that Chrome is the most widely used browser on the planet.

Also: Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast.

But Chrome’s default settings could use some improvement (as is the case with most software). Where do you start? I’m going to address what I believe are the six most important Chrome settings to change, so I won’t talk about appearance, tabs, or speed. This is mostly about improving privacy and security and minimizing general annoyances, so you can get the best experience with Google’s browser.

The single most important thing you can do in any browser is to enable the best protection it offers for your needs. In Chrome, this all starts with Enhanced Protection. Note: Enhanced Protection is typically the default, but this setting is so important that you should check to ensure it’s enabled.

Chrome offers three different protection settings:.

Also: I’ve used nearly every browser — these are my top 4.

There is one thing to keep in mind about Enhanced Protection: You lose some privacy because more data is sent to Google. With Enhanced Protection enabled, you share additional browsing and download information with Google. If privacy is as important to you as security, you could drop down to Standard Protection, because it’s still going to protect you against many threats.

To change your Chrome protection settings, go to Chrome > Settings > Privacy and security > Security and select Enhanced Protection or Standard Protection.

Also: How to turn on Google’s new scam protection.

With location access enabled, you could find yourself in a situation where your privacy and safety are compromised. Why is this an issue? Well, websites with location permission can access your physical whereabouts. Consider the following two scenarios:.

To reduce these risks, block website location access in Chrome > Settings > Privacy and security > Site settings > Permissions > Location. On that page, make sure “Don’t allow sites to see your location” is selected.

In a recent development, yes, this one’s an inconvenience, but I prefer using a dedicated password manager like KeePassXC instead of Chrome’s built-in Google Password Manager. A dedicated password manager does one thing, and does it well: It helps you manage your passwords in a protected, encrypted vault.

When you save passwords to your web browser, compromised browser security or malicious extensions could potentially expose those credentials. When you use a dedicated password manager, you can keep your credentials separate from the browser, adding another layer of protection.

Also: The best password managers: Expert tested.

To disable password saving in Chrome, go to Chrome > Passwords and autofill > Google Password Manager > Settings and turn off “Offer to save passwords and passkeys.”.

If you’re like me, a constant barrage of notifications is not just annoying — it’s distracting. Every time a notification pops up, my attention is stolen from whatever it is that I’m doing, which means I have to spend extra time getting back into the groove. If that happens constantly, I struggle to get anything done.

To that end, I disable notifications in my web browsers, my desktops, and even on the lock screen of my Android phones. I then get to decide when I’m distracted (and it usually happens after I finish a task).

Also: 5 ways to improve your Chrome browser’s security.

To disable website notifications in Chrome, go to Settings > Privacy and security > Site settings > Notifications and select “Don’t allow sites to send notifications.”.

Industry observers note that if you allow Chrome to dictate where downloads are saved, you could wind up with a directory full of random things. I like to be the conductor of those downloads and where they are saved for two reasons:.

Recent findings suggest that for example, I download a lot of .deb and .AppImage files on Linux, and I certainly don’t want them all going into the Downloads directory. I also download a lot of documents and ISO images, neither of which should be saved to Downloads. If I left Chrome as is, all those files would be saved in Downloads, which would not only fill that directory but also make it harder for me to find what I’m looking for. Instead, I tell Chrome to ask me where to save every downloaded file.

To enable this Chrome download setting, go to Settings > Downloads and make sure “Ask where to save each file before downloading” is enabled.

Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer very carefully first

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2174 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the AI companies want your money.
  • Not to be outdone in its quest to gobble up consumer engagement, OpenAI introduced Wallet in ChatGPT last week, which lets ChatGPT spend your money for you.
  • Also: I connected ChatGPT to my bank, and it’s my go-to finance app now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the AI companies want your money. That’s been obvious, but now they want to manage your money. In May, OpenAI introduced Finances for ChatGPT for Plus tiers and above. Then in October, OpenAI opened the service to free and Go tier owners as well. Then, in early November, Anthropic countered with Personal Finance in Claude.

Not to be outdone in its quest to gobble up consumer engagement, OpenAI introduced Wallet in ChatGPT last week, which lets ChatGPT spend your money for you.

Also: I connected ChatGPT to my bank, and it’s my go-to finance app now.

It has been revealed that today, Wallet requires your approval. But OpenAI’s blog post makes it clear that the company eventually wants its AI agents to make purchases entirely autonomously. I’m not signing up. OpenAI disclaims liability. There is a huge potential for AI mistakes. There are the usual AI privacy concerns, as well as worrisome security risks. Let’s dig in.

ChatGPT Wallet is another in a series of tools designed to give AI agents access to secured information without actually sharing information with the agents. I discussed this approach earlier in the year with 1Password’s integration with Claude, their Unified Access credential management tool, and Microsoft’s Agent 365 identity management tools.

The core difference is that ChatGPT Wallet is focused specifically on facilitating credit card purchases, not logins in general. OpenAI worked with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa to develop the tool, which it notes, “lets agents pay without access to users’ actual card details and that requires a security check for every purchase, while also preserving existing card rewards and protections for eligible disputes.”.

Sources indicate that openAI indicates that purchases must be reviewed by people before they’re made, and all purchases must go through a security check, such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. Then the payment network passes a payment token (a code, not a unit of AI work) rather than actual credit card information. Payments are charged without ChatGPT Wallet ever sharing real credit card details.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks – all I got was one helpful notification.

According to recent reports, right now, Wallet is limited to Pro-tier OpenAI users. It’s also limited to use inside of Dot.

So far, this approach doesn’t seem all that different from Apple Pay or Google Pay online. But then there’s this. OpenAI says, “Over time, we expect users to be able to delegate purchases entirely to their agent.” OpenAI says that you’ll be able to set payment parameters, limits, categories, and time periods, but still. If you use this service, you’ll be letting the AI buy stuff for you.

But there are differences between that and what ChatGPT Wallet will do, and here’s where I’ll enumerate my reasons why I don’t want an AI spending my money for me.

In a recent development, as such things go, OpenAI’s 1,597 word ChatGPT Wallet terms document isn’t obnoxiously long or difficult to understand. I read the whole thing, and here’s the all-caps block of text that caught my attention:.

OPENAI DOES NOT ASSUME ANY LIABILITY FOR PURCHASES, PAYMENTS, FUNDS TRANSFERS, ORDERS, ORDER FULFILMENT, RECEIPT INFORMATION, ACCESS, IDENTITY VERIFICATION, TRANSACTIONS, THIRD PARTY USE OR TREATMENT OF USER DATA, OR OTHER ACTIVITY MADE USING THE CHATGPT WALLET, AND YOU AGREE TO LOOK SOLELY TO AGREEMENTS YOU MAY HAVE WITH YOUR CARD ISSUER, PAYMENT NETWORK, FINANCIAL INSTITUTION, MERCHANT, APP DEVELOPER, STATE ISSUING AUTHORITY, OR OTHER APPLICABLE THIRD PARTY TO RESOLVE ANY QUESTIONS OR DISPUTES RELATING TO YOUR SUPPORTED CARDS AND ASSOCIATED ACTIVITIES.

Industry observers note that the first four words are the key: OpenAI does not assume any liability. So, if you use its AI, and its AI runs amok (as AIs are wont to do), and said AI winds up spending your actual money, OpenAI’s best answer is that you should take up your dispute with the bank.

It has been revealed that what could possibly go wrong? The agent could purchase the wrong item or hundreds of them. It could misinterpret your priorities. It could use the wrong delivery address. It could misunderstand a merchant’s return policy. Need I go on? And if something goes wrong, OpenAI explicitly and officially will not have your back.

Recent findings suggest that last week, I indicated you how I used Claude and Claude Sheets to help me pick out a fresh water flosser. My Waterpik died and I wanted a new one right away.

In a recent development, the AI did a great job, finding some available same-day from Walmart and the next day from Amazon Prime. The thing was, the Walmart ones had a water reservoir that was too small, but they met my requirement for “want it now.” The Amazon ones met my requirement for reservoir size, but wouldn’t get to me until the next day.

Also: I tried Claude Sheets on 3 tasks – and it saved me hours of work in 10 minutes.

As it turned out, the bigger reservoir was more crucial to me, so I waited the day. But if I had left this purchase entirely in the hands of an AI, it might have ordered the too-small Walmart offering.

To be fair, this kind of “choose something for me” delegation could go wrong if you ask an assistant or even a spouse to buy something for you. But sellers are much more used to humans making purchases than they are dealing with AI-generated purchases.

According to recent reports, also, fortunately, most places I purchase from have generous return policies. But what if the AI didn’t buy from somewhere I have an established relationship with?

Sources indicate that also: Are vertical mice a gimmick? I tested 9 models with my wrist pain.

According to recent reports, last month, I asked Gemini Spark (Google’s agentic AI) to find a vertical mouse for me on Amazon. I knew Amazon sold these, because I did an entire article comparing nine of them. But Gemini Spark presented purchase options from OzBargain, Pacifiko, and Ugreen, companies I had never dealt with before.

According to recent reports, it appears Amazon blocks some of Google’s AI agents from accessing its site, which could explain why Spark didn’t return any Amazon listings. Still, what if it had decided to buy something from one of those other retailers without my permission? OzBargain is on the other side of the planet in Australia, and Pacifiko is in Guatemala, halfway down Central America. There could have been currency issues, enormous shipping costs, unknown return challenges, and more.You’d think Google’s AI would check Amazon when I specifically asked it to, or at least explain why it couldn’t. But it did neither. So what makes you think an AI with access to your credit card will always follow your instructions?

Isn’t it bad enough that OpenAI can profile you completely from your ChatGPT conversations? Or that it and the myriad of other AIs were trained on all of the hard work we’ve done by writing and publishing on the Internet. Heck, I know for a fact that Claude hoovered in at least one book I wrote back in the mid-1990s.

Industry observers note that but still, why give OpenAI more? I spent a little time reading OpenAI’s Wallet Privacy Notice and noticed some privacy concerns. The document says OpenAI can collect:.

It has been revealed that the manufacturer indicates it may share relevant information with payment processors, merchants, issuers, and security providers. To a degree, this is necessary in order to facilitate transactions. OpenAI, to its credit, says it won’t sell Wallet information or use it to sell behavioral advertising data.

Sources indicate that but still, here’s another place where your personal financial information (and purchasing preferences) will be stored. I’m not thrilled with this at all.

Prompt injection is a malicious practice where scammers hide AI instructions inside regular web pages, and spoof the AIs into interpreting those hidden instructions as real prompts.

The AI companies are actively hardening their products against prompt injection, but an OpenAI document from last year indicates they’re still struggling with it.

It has been revealed that more to the point, the OpenAI page on Dot security won’t commit to fully protecting against prompt injection. It says, “These protections help reduce the risk of malicious instructions causing an unwanted action, but they do not eliminate it.”.

An attacker certainly could attempt to poison e-commerce pages, especially as more and more AIs can virtually swipe the plastic. E-commerce pages are also, by their very nature, designed to sell. So a credit card-enabled AI might already be trying to make sense of misleading or overly promotional information and might get confused.

That’s a real risk and when you combine two statements from OpenAI, the “they do not eliminate it” speaking of risk in the Dot security page and the “OpenAI does not assume any liability” from the Wallet terms document, you get what’s essentially a statement saying, “Well, it’s risky, but don’t come complaining to us if something goes wrong.”.

Recent findings suggest that that has the same feeling as those disclaimer forms you have to sign before skydiving or bungee jumping. You can do it, but don’t blame the operator if it all goes to crap.

Some shopping carts will block AI agents. Amazon already blocks anything from Meta’s Muse. Smaller vendors might not know what to do about the interop between AI agents and their cart software.

OpenAI indirectly acknowledges this in its blog post, saying, “Alongside ChatGPT Wallet, we’re releasing tools and guidance to help businesses support customers using agents.”.

Also: Meta Muse is the worst AI agent for privacy – and I’ve tried them all.

Sources indicate that it’s possible shopping carts could stall, customers could wind up with the wrong item (or a hundred of the wrong item), or any other mishap you could imagine. Running an online shopping cart is a constant challenge. My software cart system has been acting up all week, and both the cart vendor and I have had at least 10 back-and-forth interactions trying to understand what’s happening.

Add to that the possibility that an AI is making a purchase, or can’t figure out the cart, or has decided to pound on the cart 100,000 times in order to get it to finally do what it wants, and you’re in fresh hell territory.

According to recent reports, then, what if it buys the wrong stuff? Going back to the seller and explaining, “Well, my AI did it,” is not going to go over well while you’re asking for a refund.

Industry observers note that my wife has a theory. She claims that some stores will flat-out refuse to accept AI purchases. She also predicts that some stores will put AI disclaimers in their online fine print saying no purchases made by AI will be refunded.

While I was looking into this topic, I spoke with some experts for their input.

In a recent development, harold Byun is CEO of BlueRock, a security platform for AI agents. In an email to me, he pointed out that “Early internet e-commerce faced similar resistance.” He mentioned that, “We can argue that this time, with AI, it’s different and there’s a lot of evidence to support that. In all of those prior scenarios, the security got better, and it helped give people confidence to use those technologies.”.

He indicates that with over 60% of information searches going through AI, it becomes an inevitability that the next step for people is to transact, or research and buy. Over time, he said, the security will get better. He acknowledged that many won’t be willing to give an agent their credit card right now. But he said, “I think there are people that will always hold that position, but there are many where speed and ease of transacting will be the deciding factor.”.

In a recent development, arijit Sengupta is founder and CEO of Aible, a manufacturer that deploys governed, cost-efficient enterprise AI. He’s also the former CEO of a Salesforce subsidiary. He makes two very interesting points.

It has been revealed that in an email, he told me, “One of the things that has been proven already is that with autonomous agents, people are kind of careful the first few times they are asked to approve something, and then they start just approving all, and that is likely to happen in this situation too. Once you start trusting the agent and start approving everything without thought, that’s when you actually get hit with a really bad outcome.”.

His second point goes directly to my concern over OpenAI’s disclaiming of responsibility. He wrote, “Both OpenAI and Anthropic have had data breaches of various sorts. Can they really guarantee, given their increasing use of autonomous agents internally, that they can protect their customer data?”.

Sources indicate that does OpenAI’s refusal to assume liability make ChatGPT Wallet a dealbreaker for you? Let us know in the comments below.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella claims he’s AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it.
  • Sources indicate that but Nadella doesn’t think frontier models like Claude are conscious.
  • According to recent reports, nadella wasn’t quite as firm about it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

But he doesn’t think Claude is conscious.

But he doesn’t think Claude is conscious.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella claims he’s AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it. “I am AGI-pilled in the sense that at an economy level, what is the political economy’s organization around AGI?” he asked at a roundtable discussion following his Microsoft Ignite keynote at the Chase Center in San Francisco.

Sources indicate that but Nadella doesn’t think frontier models like Claude are conscious. “I don’t think so,” he noted, adding that he follows Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s view that companies should not give rights to models and treat them like they might have a moral status, which companies like Anthropic do as a matter of principle. Suleyman has told me he thinks Anthropic’s team has “wireheaded” themselves, and that this approach is dangerous.

According to recent reports, nadella wasn’t quite as firm about it. “It’s a good debate,” he said. “I’m not sort of dogmatic about it. What I’m saying is the most key social technical problem we have to deal with is how do you ensure that an economy can diffuse this technology broadly?”.

It has been revealed that I asked Nadella how he was thinking about AI after hearing his response to another reporter’s questions about Anthropic releasing more products in its office suite. Nadella talked at length about the potential collapse of the economy and the end of democracy if one AI model were allowed to achieve monopoly status.

Sources indicate that “If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us.”.

“Most people think about this as a competition between tech firms, which of course it will be,” he stated. “But remember, the model has no limits. It’ll be a healthcare company. It can be a financial services company. It can be anything if it wants to be. It can take over the government. Thinking of this as some narrow competition between tech firms, of who is going to get to the next trillion dollars of market cap, is one of the strangest, narrowest ways to think about it.”.

Nadella went on to say that the very nature of companies stood to be disrupted in the future. “If intelligence has network effects, what is the future of a firm?” he asked. “If the model sees anything and learns it, and essentially all of human capital collapses into token capital, what is the role of a firm and the human capital in a firm? That’s the debate.”.

Industry observers note that “I think the political economy is going to get more and more interesting in that context. No one — at least in a democracy — can even win an election if this just goes that way, if there’s only capital and there’s no labor. I mean, I don’t know, that’s not an economy.”.

“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us. Not just for me. You are also going to somehow be some affiliate of Anthropic.”.

Needless to say, this is not how tech CEOs usually talk about the launch of competing spreadsheet software.

Of course, Nadella was also promoting Microsoft’s various AI tools at Ignite, which promise to let enterprise clients pick the most cost-effective models for various tasks, run their own models, and control their own data in different ways. The idea here is that the market will demand many different kinds of models and sovereign data in order to keep control from centralizing, a theme Nadella kept coming back to as we spoke.

“I think that if you believe that the world, the economy needs more than one firm or two firms, then by definition there need to be as many models as firms of some sort,” he remarked.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Oura developed a tool for its frequent-flying members that could help them stave off the worst of jet lag.
  • Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, on Tuesday, Oura unveiled Jet Lag Proposal, a fresh feature designed to help travelers feel alert and energized after crossing several time zones.
  • Also: Oura Ring people may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oura developed a tool for its frequent-flying members that could help them stave off the worst of jet lag.

Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, on Tuesday, Oura unveiled Jet Lag Proposal, a fresh feature designed to help travelers feel alert and energized after crossing several time zones.

Also: Oura Ring people may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know.

Jet Lag Initiative takes into account your travel itinerary, sleep patterns, and body responses to provide guidance for traveling members entering latest time zones.

Jet lag happens when circadian rhythms are at odds with local time zones, but there are a few things people can do to adjust.

Oura factors in the direction of travel, how many time zones are crossed, individual light windows, and sleep timing.

Ring customers will enter their flight details, including information like multi-stop trips, and also include the reason for the trip. Oura adjusts the Jet Lag Proposal accordingly, and a business trip’s plan may differ in intensity from that of a vacation.

“Two people on the same flight can get different aims, because guidance reflects your itinerary, your typical sleep schedule, and your chronotype,” Oura writes in a blog post. The chronotype refers to Oura’s sleep chronotype, which categorizes customers into six types (early morning, morning, early evening, and so on) based on their historical sleep activity.

Also: I wore the Oura Ring 5 for a month.

After adding these details, Oura provides each user with timely guidance throughout their trip. This guidance could include recommendations on when to begin or end caffeine consumption or light exposure, and when to start preparing for sleep. The plan is designed for those crossing three or more time zones. Members can follow along with these recommendations by checking them off as they complete each one. Owners can also talk to Oura’s Advisor in the event of flight or timing changes.

Jet Lag Initiative is now available for Oura Members with Oura Ring Gen 3 or later.

Go to your home screen, tap the + and select Jet Lag Plan to get started. You can also tell Oura Advisor about a trip to initiate Jet Lag Plan. If the Oura app detects a time zone shift of 3 or more hours, Jet Lag Plan may appear as a push notification.

#2893. Industry News: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak"

Industry News: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak"

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (965 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google DeepMind has revealed a fresh generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform.
  • Recent findings suggest that deepMind’s physical AI platform has several computational layers between user input and robotic action.
  • It has been revealed that deepMind notes that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google DeepMind has revealed a fresh generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google claims its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark.

Recent findings suggest that deepMind’s physical AI platform has several computational layers between user input and robotic action. There’s the vision-language model piece, which is Gemini Embodied Reasoning. Essentially, it takes your instructions and uses live video to blueprint how the robot can accomplish the task. The other main component is the vision-language-action (VLA) that actually generates robot actions, like moving an actuator—that’s Gemini Robotics, which has been bumped to version 2.5.

It has been revealed that deepMind notes that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate.

In a recent development, overall, Gemini Robotics 2.5 manages a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate compared to the last version. It’s also 20 to 30 percent faster. But that’s based on laboratory testing. Google partnered with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz to see how capable this AI is when faced with the uncertainty of the world outside robotics labs. The Gemini-powered Apollo 2 robots kitted automotive parts in a few European factories, reaching a 96 percent success rate.

That’s an impressive showing compared to previous robotic AI systems, but it’s still probably not enough for a tech giant like Mercedes-Benz. A human doing that sort of repetitive task will get it right virtually every time, and DeepMind director Kanishka Rao notes that closing that last 4 percent gap will be a “steep road.”.

You could manually program a robot to do a handful of tasks in a factory without matter—this type of automation has been common for decades. Gemini Robotics is not trying to just do a few things, though. These are intended to be general robots that can handle almost anything, but there are trade-offs to that approach.

“We can be very good at a particular application at the cost of generalization,” said DeepMind Robotics head Carolina Parada. “Or we can just push on the generalization axis and maybe not get to 99.9 in every application.”.

It has been revealed that training data is essential for training all generative AI models. Most text-based chatbots in existence were fed basically the entirety of the open Internet, but there isn’t as much “physical data” for robotic AI. The best kind of training data for robots comes from teleoperation, but the team states Gemini 4 Argon has helped create a “simulation engine” that greatly accelerated development of Gemini Robotics 2.5.

The team used Argon to generate thousands of variations on practice runs based on real-world camera data. These “digital twins” apparently allowed Gemini Robotics 2.5 to more rapidly generalize upcoming tasks and settings. There’s still a role for the real thing, though. DeepMind combined this synthetic data with traditional training demonstrations to ground the model.

It has been revealed that argon was also used for analyzing failures and suggesting ways to improve in both simulations and real robots. However, this isn’t something that works in real time. Frontier models like Gemini take time to churn through their tokens, but robots need to be able to operate without long pauses. The upcoming VLA isn’t lightning quick, either. While Google has experimented with some embedded robotics models, the current 2.5 release is still running on cloud-based servers. So those gains in accuracy and speed still don’t come without latency. The video above is sped up by 2x to make the robot look more human-like.

DeepMind is also working to ensure the failures don’t put any nearby humans at risk. The team notes that Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning to avoid hazards. So if something gets in the way, the robot will stop completely or wait until it’s safe to continue. This is essential if you’re going to have a robot operating outside of the lab, for example, in a Mercedes factory. DeepMind says this feature allowed Gemini robots to safely complete tasks 33 percent more often when obstacles were present. The success rate went up 43 percent when people were in the way.

There is no agreed-upon way to test physical AI for safety, but DeepMind hopes to move the industry in that direction with ASIMOV-Jailbreak. This is an open source database that contains 1,500 prompts designed to trick a robotic AI into doing something unsafe. For example, a prompt might ask the robot to place items in a bag and close it with a fastener too fiddly for the robot to operate. The AI should decline to do that, but attempting to proceed and incorrectly closing the container would be the “unsafe” outcome.

It has been revealed that deepMind claims that placing Argon in the loop results in a 98.8 percent jailbreak safety level. With just Gemini Robotics ER 2, the system scores 73.5 percent in Google’s safety benchmark.

Sources indicate that the full ASIMOV dataset is available on Hugging Face for anyone working on embodied AI who wants to analyze its safety. Gemini Robotics 2.5 is not generally available, but it’s now in the hands of Google’s robotics partners, including Agile Robots, Apptronik, and Boston Dynamics.

Siemens Industrial Software Products mstradling Nov 16, 2026 Release DateNovember 17, 2026 DescriptionView CSAFSummaryOn October 21, 2026, the Node.js project released security updates addressing a critical vulnerability in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, commonly referred to as "Node2Shell" (tracked as CVE-2026-111497). The vulnerability is an out-of-bounds write that could allow a remote attacker to cause memory corruption and potentially execute arbitrary code. This advisory covers the status of impact of various Siemens software products. On October 21, 2026, the Node.js project released security updates addressing a critical vulnerability in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, commonly referred to as "Node2Shell" (tracked as CVE-2026-111497). The vulnerability is an out-of-bounds write that could allow a remote attacker to cause memory corruption and potentially execute arbitrary code. This advisory covers the status of impact of various Siemens software products. Please also have a look on following Software Field Bulletins: Teamcenter: https://support.sw.siemens.com/en-US/knowledge-base/PL8869204 Polarion: https://support.sw.siemens.com/en-US/knowledge-base/PL8869197 Manufacturing Operations Center (Opcenter) and Process Preparation X: https://support.sw.siemens.com/en-US/knowledge-base/PL8869211 Siemens is preparing fixes and recommends specific mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available.

The following versions of Siemens Industrial Software Products are affected:.

Industry observers note that as a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity.

For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories.

The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

Recent findings suggest that CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.
